~~~python
# src/rush/tools/pbt.py::PbtTool.run. Selection uses exact @given import
# aliases; pytest collection then verifies selected node IDs before run.
import ast
import re
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
def discover_given_nodes(source, relative_path):
    tree = ast.parse(source)
    direct = {alias.asname or alias.name for node in tree.body
              if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module == "hypothesis"
              for alias in node.names if alias.name == "given"}
    module = {alias.asname or alias.name for node in tree.body
              if isinstance(node, ast.Import) for alias in node.names
              if alias.name == "hypothesis"}
    found = []
    for node in tree.body:
        if not isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef): continue
        for decorator in node.decorator_list:
            callee = decorator.func if isinstance(decorator, ast.Call) else decorator
            if (isinstance(callee, ast.Name) and callee.id in direct or
                isinstance(callee, ast.Attribute) and callee.attr == "given" and
                isinstance(callee.value, ast.Name) and callee.value.id in module):
                found.append(f"{relative_path}::{node.name}")
                break
    return found
def pbt_argv(pytest_bin, node_ids, seed, junit_path):
    if type(seed) is not int or seed < 0 or not node_ids:
        raise ValueError("invalid_property_selection")
    return [pytest_bin, "--hypothesis-seed=" + str(seed),
            "--hypothesis-show-statistics", "--junitxml=" + str(junit_path), *node_ids]
def property_receipt(stdout, junit_xml, exit_code):
    try:
        root = ET.fromstring(junit_xml)
        suites = [root] if root.tag == "testsuite" else root.findall("testsuite")
        collected = sum(int(s.get("tests", "0")) for s in suites)
    except (ET.ParseError, ValueError):
        return {"status":"error","reason":"malformed_junit"}
    counts = [int(n) for n in re.findall(r"\b(\d+) (?:passing|failing) examples?\b", stdout)]
    if collected == 0: return {"status":"skipped","reason":"zero_property_tests"}
    if not counts: return {"status":"error","reason":"missing_hypothesis_statistics"}
    return {"status":"fail" if exit_code else "ok",
            "tests_collected":collected,"generated_examples":sum(counts)}
# `shrinks` and exact counterexample are not supplied by this parser; leave
# them null/incomplete unless a version-bound Hypothesis receipt supplies both.
~~~

~~~python
# src/rush/tools/pbt.py::PbtTool.run
from pathlib import Path
from secrets import randbits
def select_property_nodes(path, test_paths=()):
    if test_paths: return list(test_paths)
    path = Path(path)
    files = [path] if path.is_file() else sorted(path.rglob("test_*.py"))
    return [node for file in files
            for node in discover_given_nodes(file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
                                             file.as_posix())]
def selected_pbt_argv(pytest_bin, path, test_paths, requested_seed, fresh_junit):
    selected = select_property_nodes(path, test_paths)
    seed = requested_seed if requested_seed is not None else randbits(64)
    return pbt_argv(pytest_bin, selected, seed, fresh_junit), seed
~~~

~~~python
# src/rush/tools/visual.py::VisualTool.run. Engine commands verified against
# https://github.com/lost-pixel/lost-pixel/blob/main/docs/community-edition/testing-and-updating-baseline-locally.md
# and https://github.com/garris/BackstopJS#the-backstopjs-workflow .
from hashlib import sha256
def visual_plan(binary, engine_name, operation, *, browser=False, accept=False,
                artifact_write=False, changed_baselines=()):
    if not browser: raise PermissionError("browser_denied")
    if operation not in {"compare","update"}: raise ValueError("unknown_operation")
    if engine_name not in {"lost-pixel","backstop"}: raise ValueError("unknown_engine")
    if operation == "compare": return [binary,"test"]
    if not accept or not artifact_write: raise PermissionError("baseline_update_denied")
    if not changed_baselines: raise ValueError("no_reviewed_diff")
    return [binary,"update" if engine_name == "lost-pixel" else "approve"]
def baseline_result(before, after, *, operation, compare_exit, update_exit=None):
    changed = sorted(k for k in before.keys() | after.keys() if before.get(k) != after.get(k))
    if operation == "compare" and changed:
        return {"status":"error","reason":"compare_mutated_baseline","changed":changed}
    if operation == "update" and update_exit:
        return {"status":"error","reason":"update_failed","changed":changed}
    return {"status":"fail" if compare_exit and operation == "compare" else "ok",
            "changed":changed,"baseline_mutated":bool(changed)}
def visual_identity(engine_version, viewport, config_bytes, baseline_hashes):
    if not viewport: raise ValueError("viewport_required")
    payload = repr((engine_version,viewport,sha256(config_bytes).hexdigest(),
                    sorted(baseline_hashes.items()))).encode("utf-8")
    return sha256(payload).hexdigest()
# At callsite: compare first with resolved engine; parse fresh diff report and
# reject unknown/missing baseline paths. Update only reviewed changed set under
# same config/viewport identity; take baseline digests before/after, reject any
# changed path outside reviewed set, and include fresh version from `--version`.
~~~

**Correction — complete proposed fix route supersedes helper-only callsite comment above:** Replace `VisualTool.run` with the route below and add `baseline_paths` plus `reviewed_baselines` keyword lists to `VisualTool.__call__`, catalog CLI, and MCP. Existing helpers remain usable inside this route; their standalone assertions prove only planning rules.

~~~python
def run(
    self,
    path: Path,
    *,
    operation: str = "compare",
    accept: bool = False,
    baseline_paths: list[str] | None = None,
    reviewed_baselines: list[str] | None = None,
    permissions=None,
    **options: object,
) -> ToolResult:
    from hashlib import sha256
    from rush.engines.backstop import BackstopEngine
    from rush.engines.lost_pixel import LostPixelEngine
    from rush.io.physical_paths import PhysicalRoot
    from rush.permissions import ExecutionPermissions, build_execution_metadata, check_permissions

    started = now_ms()
    if operation not in {"compare", "update"} or type(accept) is not bool:
        return error_result(self.name, None, "invalid visual operation or accept value")
    required = ExecutionPermissions(browser=True, artifact_write=operation == "update")
    allowed, missing = check_permissions(required, permissions)
    if not allowed or operation == "update" and not accept:
        reason = ",".join(missing) if missing else "accept"
        return skipped_result(self.name, None, f"visual operation denied: {reason}")

    root = (path if path.is_dir() else path.parent).resolve()
    physical = PhysicalRoot(root)
    names = baseline_paths or []
    reviewed = set(reviewed_baselines or [])
    if not names or operation == "update" and (not reviewed or not reviewed <= set(names)):
        return error_result(self.name, None, "contained baseline_paths and reviewed_baselines required")

    def digests() -> dict[str, str]:
        values: dict[str, str] = {}
        for name in names:
            baseline = physical.open_contained(name, purpose="read")
            if not baseline.is_file():
                raise ValueError(f"baseline missing: {name}")
            values[name] = sha256(baseline.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        return values

    binary = resolve_binary("lost-pixel") or resolve_binary("backstop")
    if not binary:
        return skipped_result(self.name, "lost-pixel/backstop", "visual engine not found on PATH")
    engine_name = "lost-pixel" if Path(binary).name.startswith("lost-pixel") else "backstop"
    engine = LostPixelEngine() if engine_name == "lost-pixel" else BackstopEngine()
    before = digests()
    compare = run_subprocess([binary, "test"], cwd=root, timeout=180.0)
    after_compare = digests()
    if after_compare != before:
        return error_result(self.name, engine_name, "compare mutated baseline")
    if operation == "compare":
        status = "ok" if compare.returncode == 0 else "fail"
        return ToolResult(tool=self.name, engine=engine_name, engine_version=engine.version(),
            status=status, duration_ms=elapsed_ms(started),
            summary=f"visual compare completed with status '{status}'", findings=[],
            raw=compare.stdout, metadata={"operation":"compare","baseline_mutated":False,
                "baseline_digests":before,
                "execution":build_execution_metadata("executed",granted=permissions)})
    if compare.returncode == 0:
        return error_result(self.name, engine_name, "no fresh visual diff to approve")

    update_verb = "update" if engine_name == "lost-pixel" else "approve"
    updated = run_subprocess([binary, update_verb], cwd=root, timeout=180.0)
    after_update = digests()
    changed = sorted(name for name in names if before[name] != after_update[name])
    if updated.returncode != 0 or not changed or set(changed) - reviewed:
        return error_result(self.name, engine_name, "baseline update failed or changed unreviewed baseline")
    return ToolResult(tool=self.name, engine=engine_name, engine_version=engine.version(),
        status="ok", duration_ms=elapsed_ms(started),
        summary=f"visual update changed {len(changed)} reviewed baseline(s)", findings=[],
        raw=updated.stdout, metadata={"operation":"update","changed_baselines":changed,
            "baseline_digests_before":before,"baseline_digests_after":after_update,
            "execution":build_execution_metadata("executed",granted=permissions)})
~~~

It invokes `VisualTool.run` four times and asserts: no child without browser grant; compare with browser grant calls `test` without accept and preserves digest; update with browser plus artifact-write but `accept=False` calls no child; update with both grants calls `test` then `approve`, returns `status="ok"`, records exact before/after digests, and reports `changed_baselines == ["baseline/card.png"]`. A second fixture makes `approve` alter `baseline/unreviewed.png` and expects `status="error"`. This exercises full proposed `VisualTool.run`, child dispatch, permission split, and file-effect verification.

~~~python
def test_compare_and_update_use_distinct_permissioned_routes(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    from types import SimpleNamespace
    from rush.permissions import ExecutionPermissions
    from rush.tools.visual import VisualTool

    baseline = tmp_path / "baseline"
    baseline.mkdir()
    card = baseline / "card.png"
    other = baseline / "unreviewed.png"
    card.write_bytes(b"old-card")
    other.write_bytes(b"old-other")
    calls = []
    mutate_unreviewed = False

    def child(argv, **kwargs):
        calls.append(list(argv))
        if argv[1] == "approve":
            card.write_bytes(b"new-card")
            if mutate_unreviewed:
                other.write_bytes(b"new-other")
            return SimpleNamespace(returncode=0, stdout="approved", stderr="")
        assert argv[1] == "test"
        return SimpleNamespace(returncode=1, stdout='{"tests":[]}', stderr="")

    monkeypatch.setattr("rush.tools.visual.resolve_binary", lambda name: "/fixture/backstop" if name == "backstop" else None)
    monkeypatch.setattr("rush.tools.visual.run_subprocess", child)
    monkeypatch.setattr("rush.engines.backstop.BackstopEngine.version", lambda self: "6.3.25")
    tool = VisualTool()
    paths = ["baseline/card.png", "baseline/unreviewed.png"]

    denied = tool.run(tmp_path, operation="compare", baseline_paths=paths)
    assert denied["status"] == "skipped" and calls == []
    compared = tool.run(tmp_path, operation="compare", baseline_paths=paths,
        permissions=ExecutionPermissions(browser=True))
    assert compared["status"] == "fail" and calls[-1][1] == "test"
    assert card.read_bytes() == b"old-card" and other.read_bytes() == b"old-other"
    call_count = len(calls)
    denied_update = tool.run(tmp_path, operation="update", accept=False,
        baseline_paths=paths, reviewed_baselines=["baseline/card.png"],
        permissions=ExecutionPermissions(browser=True, artifact_write=True))
    assert denied_update["status"] == "skipped" and len(calls) == call_count
    updated = tool.run(tmp_path, operation="update", accept=True,
        baseline_paths=paths, reviewed_baselines=["baseline/card.png"],
        permissions=ExecutionPermissions(browser=True, artifact_write=True))
    assert [argv[1] for argv in calls[-2:]] == ["test", "approve"]
    assert updated["status"] == "ok"
    assert updated["metadata"]["changed_baselines"] == ["baseline/card.png"]
    assert updated["metadata"]["baseline_digests_before"] != updated["metadata"]["baseline_digests_after"]

    card.write_bytes(b"old-card")
    other.write_bytes(b"old-other")
    mutate_unreviewed = True
    rejected = tool.run(tmp_path, operation="update", accept=True,
        baseline_paths=paths, reviewed_baselines=["baseline/card.png"],
        permissions=ExecutionPermissions(browser=True, artifact_write=True))
    assert rejected["status"] == "error"
~~~

~~~python
from hashlib import sha256
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from rush.engines.base import Engine
from rush.patch.applier import PatchApplier
from rush.patch.sandbox import PatchSandboxManager
from rush.patch_generator import patch_target_paths


def _visual_failure_ids(engine_name: str, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> frozenset[str]:
    findings = raw.get("findings")
    if not isinstance(findings, list):
        raise ValueError("visual engine omitted findings list")
    identities: set[str] = set()
    for item in findings:
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            raise ValueError("visual engine emitted non-object finding")
        if engine_name == "backstop":
            pair = item.get("pair")
            if not isinstance(pair, dict):
                raise ValueError("backstop finding omitted pair")
            parts = (pair.get("label"), pair.get("viewportLabel"), pair.get("url"))
        elif engine_name == "lost-pixel":
            parts = (item.get("storyId"), item.get("name"))
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported visual engine: {engine_name}")
        if not all(isinstance(value, str) and value for value in parts):
            raise ValueError("visual finding omitted stable identity field")
        identities.add("\x1f".join(parts))
    return frozenset(identities)


def run_css_cause_trial(
    repo_root: Path,
    unified_diff: str,
    engine: Engine,
    engine_args: list[str],
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    targets = patch_target_paths(unified_diff)
    css_suffixes = {".css", ".scss", ".sass", ".less"}
    if not targets or any(Path(target).suffix.lower() not in css_suffixes for target in targets):
        raise ValueError("trial patch must contain CSS-family files only")
    manager = PatchSandboxManager(repo_root)
    sandboxes: list[Path] = []
    try:
        baseline_sandbox = manager.create_sandbox()
        sandboxes.append(baseline_sandbox)
        candidate_sandbox = manager.create_sandbox()
        sandboxes.append(candidate_sandbox)
        before_raw = engine.run(baseline_sandbox, engine_args, cwd=baseline_sandbox)
        before_ids = _visual_failure_ids(engine.name, before_raw)
        if not before_ids:
            return {"status": "rejected", "reason": "no_original_visual_failure"}
        applied, message = PatchApplier.apply_patch_to_dir(candidate_sandbox, unified_diff)
        if not applied:
            return {"status": "error", "reason": message}
        after_raw = engine.run(candidate_sandbox, engine_args, cwd=candidate_sandbox)
        after_ids = _visual_failure_ids(engine.name, after_raw)
    finally:
        for sandbox in reversed(sandboxes):
            manager.cleanup_sandbox(sandbox)

    new_ids = sorted(after_ids - before_ids)
    removed_ids = sorted(before_ids - after_ids)
    candidate = bool(removed_ids) and not new_ids and after_ids < before_ids
    return {
        "status": "candidate" if candidate else "rejected",
        "reason": "strict_failure_reduction" if candidate else "no_strict_reduction",
        "engine": engine.name,
        "engine_version": engine.version(),
        "engine_args_sha256": sha256(
            "\x00".join(engine_args).encode("utf-8")
        ).hexdigest(),
        "patch_sha256": sha256(unified_diff.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
        "before_ids": sorted(before_ids),
        "after_ids": sorted(after_ids),
        "removed_ids": removed_ids,
        "new_ids": new_ids,
    }
~~~

**Concrete interface/data flow and before/after:** CLI `rush visual . --trial-css-cause fixes/card-padding.diff --viewport mobile --allow-browser --allow-build --allow-slow --allow-artifact-write --json`; MCP carries identical typed fields. CLI/MCP → `VisualTool.run` → two verified same-HEAD worktrees → adapter/args in untouched baseline worktree → `PatchApplier.apply_patch_to_dir` in candidate worktree only → identical adapter/args in candidate → identity-set and argument-digest receipt → cleanup of both. After: candidate sandbox removes only mobile identity and leaves desktop identity; original `style.css` and original diagnostic-artifact set remain byte-identical. # src/rush/tools/snapshot.py::SnapshotTool.run
~~~python
# src/rush/tools/snapshot.py::SnapshotTool.run — exact plugin command selection.
def snapshot_argv(pytest_bin, help_text, path, junit, *, accept, plugin_name):
    if plugin_name not in {"pytest-snapshot","syrupy"}:
        raise ValueError("unsupported_snapshot_plugin")
    if "--snapshot-update" not in help_text:
        raise ValueError("snapshot_plugin_unavailable")
    return [pytest_bin, *(["--snapshot-update"] if accept else []),
            "--junitxml=" + str(junit), str(path)]
def snapshot_outcome(before, after, *, accept, artifact_write, tests_collected,
                     snapshot_tests_collected, exit_code):
    if accept and not artifact_write:
        return {"status":"skipped","reason":"permission_denied","changed":[]}
    changed = sorted(p for p in before.keys() | after.keys() if before.get(p) != after.get(p))
    if not accept and changed:
        return {"status":"error","reason":"compare_mutated_baseline","changed":changed}
    if tests_collected == 0 or snapshot_tests_collected == 0:
        return {"status":"skipped","reason":"zero_snapshot_tests","changed":changed}
    return {"status":"fail" if exit_code else "ok","changed":changed,
            "baseline_mutated":bool(changed),"tests_collected":tests_collected,
            "matched":None,"mismatched":None}
def snapshot_fixture_nodes(collected_items):
    return [item.nodeid for item in collected_items if "snapshot" in item.fixturenames]
~~~

## Command 26/79 — `rush_flaky` (Q26)

**CLI/MCP/agent-memory-token integration:** Attempts/seed/factor fields need catalog Click forwarding and matching `FlakyTool.__call__` parameters for FastMCP. Agents consume per-run transitions and controlled-factor receipts in `ToolResult`; `rush_flaky` has no current memory or token-budget path. Run IDs remain evidence locators and cannot authorize healing or substitute for matching environment/source digests.

**Use:** investigate tests with inconsistent outcomes across comparable runs. Imported JUnit mode flags repeated testcase identity regardless of outcomes (`tools/flaky.py:91–129`); duplicate/sharded records are not necessarily flaky. Execution uses `pytest --reruns 3` and returns exit-only, without per-test transition/retry evidence (`:143–201`). Catalog says report-only/no reruns (`catalog.py:374–380`).

**Fix specification:** In `src/rush/tools/flaky.py::FlakyTool.run`, replace imported duplicate-name heuristic (`:91–129`) with `analyze_imported_junit` below. Imported JUnit without distinct Rush run IDs and matching environment digests yields `repeated_unresolved`, never flaky. With those fields, classify mixed pass/fail for one testcase only; all fail is deterministic failure. Replace executed `pytest --reruns 3` exit-only path (`:177–201`) with `run_flaky_attempts` below: explicit resolved-pytest invocations, owned JUnit per run, exact argv/exit/seed/environment digest, and zero-test/collection error rejection. This avoids assuming rerun plugin availability.

**Distinct agent-side expansion (proposed; unexecuted):** `diagnose_factor` makes flakiness a controlled experiment. Current repeat run can identify mixed outcomes; it cannot separate test-order or environment sensitivity from randomness. Proposed controller chooses one permitted factor from a fixed registry (`TZ`, `PYTHONHASHSEED`, test order), runs counterbalanced A/B/B/A/A/B attempts in separate owned processes, compares outcomes for same test ID and source digest, and returns a candidate factor only when all observed failures align with one state and all passes with other. Mixed or collection-error attempts yield `inconclusive`; no automatic repair proposal follows from correlation alone.

~~~python
def factor_candidate(schedule, outcomes):
    if (len(schedule) != len(outcomes) or len(set(schedule)) != 2
        or any(value not in {"pass","fail"} for value in outcomes)):
        return "inconclusive"
    groups = {value:{outcome for state,outcome in zip(schedule,outcomes) if state==value}
              for value in set(schedule)}
    return "candidate_only" if sorted(map(tuple, map(sorted, groups.values()))) == [("fail",),("pass",)] else "inconclusive"
schedule = ["UTC","LA","LA","UTC","UTC","LA"]
assert factor_candidate(schedule, ["pass","fail","fail","pass","pass","fail"]) == "candidate_only"
assert factor_candidate(schedule, ["pass","fail","pass","pass","pass","fail"]) == "inconclusive"
assert factor_candidate(schedule, ["pass","fail","fail","pass","pass"]) == "inconclusive"
assert factor_candidate(schedule, ["pass","fail",None,"pass","pass","fail"]) == "inconclusive"
assert factor_candidate(["UTC"]*6, ["pass"]*6) == "inconclusive"
~~~

~~~python
# Add src/rush/tools/flaky.py::run_flaky_attempts.
# Called from the explicit FlakyTool.run branch below.
def run_flaky_attempts(path, *, test_paths=None, attempts=3,
                       seed=None, diagnose_factor=None, factor_values=None, permissions=None):
    import hashlib, json, os, subprocess, tempfile, time
    from xml.etree import ElementTree
    from pathlib import Path
    from ..permissions import ExecutionPermissions, check_permissions
    from ..runtime.binaries import resolve_binary
    from ..io.physical_paths import ContainmentError, PhysicalRoot
    started = time.monotonic()
    required = ExecutionPermissions(build=True, slow=True, artifact_write=True)
    allowed, missing = check_permissions(required, permissions)
    if not allowed:
        return skipped_result("flaky", "pytest", ", ".join(missing))
    if type(attempts) is not int or not 2 <= attempts <= 10:
        return error_result("flaky", "pytest", "attempts must be integer 2..10")
    if seed is not None and (type(seed) is not int or not 0 <= seed < 2**32):
        return error_result("flaky", "pytest", "seed must be uint32")
    if seed is not None and diagnose_factor == "PYTHONHASHSEED":
        return error_result("flaky", "pytest", "seed conflicts with PYTHONHASHSEED factor")
    root = (path if path.is_dir() else path.parent).resolve()
    binary = resolve_binary("pytest")
    if not binary:
        return skipped_result("flaky", "pytest", "pytest executable absent")
    try:
        physical = PhysicalRoot(root)
        selected = list(test_paths or ["." if path.is_dir() else path.name])
        if any(not isinstance(item, str) or not item or item.startswith("-") for item in selected):
            raise ValueError("invalid test paths")
        targets = []
        for item in selected:
            file, separator, node = item.partition("::")
            target = physical.open_contained(file, purpose="read")
            if not target.exists():
                raise ValueError("selected test path absent")
            targets.append(str(target) + (separator + node if separator else ""))
        if diagnose_factor is None:
            schedule = [None] * attempts
        else:
            if diagnose_factor not in {"TZ", "PYTHONHASHSEED", "order"}:
                raise ValueError("unsupported factor")
            if not isinstance(factor_values, (list, tuple)) or len(factor_values) != 2:
                raise ValueError("two factor values required")
            left, right = factor_values
            if not all(isinstance(v, str) and v and "\0" not in v for v in (left, right)) or left == right:
                raise ValueError("two distinct text values required")
            if diagnose_factor == "PYTHONHASHSEED" and any(
                not v.isdigit() or not 0 <= int(v) < 2**32 for v in (left, right)):
                raise ValueError("invalid hash seed")
            if diagnose_factor == "order" and (set((left, right)) != {"forward", "reverse"} or len(targets) < 2):
                raise ValueError("order needs two paths and forward/reverse")
            schedule = [left, right, right, left, left, right]
        source = {}
        for file in sorted(root.rglob("*.py")):
            rel = file.relative_to(root)
            if any(p.startswith(".") or p in {"node_modules", "venv"} for p in rel.parts):
                continue
            if file.is_symlink() or not file.resolve().is_relative_to(root):
                raise ValueError("source symlink refused")
            source[rel.as_posix()] = hashlib.sha256(file.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        source_digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(source, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
        runs = physical.open_contained(".rush/runs", purpose="write")
        runs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="flaky-", dir=runs))
        observations = []
        for run_id, value in enumerate(schedule):
            report = work / f"attempt-{run_id}.xml"
            env = dict(os.environ)
            env.pop("PYTHONPATH", None)
            if seed is not None:
                env["PYTHONHASHSEED"] = str(seed)
            ordered = list(targets)
            if diagnose_factor == "order" and value == "reverse":
                ordered.reverse()
            elif diagnose_factor in {"TZ", "PYTHONHASHSEED"}:
                env[diagnose_factor] = value
            argv = [binary, "-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", "--junitxml=" + str(report), *ordered]
            process = run_subprocess(argv, cwd=root, env=env, timeout=180)
            if process.returncode not in (0, 1) or not report.is_file() or report.is_symlink():
                raise ValueError(f"attempt {run_id} incomplete")
            cases = list(ElementTree.parse(report).iter("testcase"))
            if not cases or any(case.find("error") is not None for case in cases):
                raise ValueError(f"attempt {run_id} collection/setup failure")
            records = {}
            for case in cases:
                identity = (case.get("classname", ""), case.get("name", ""))
                if not identity[1] or identity in records:
                    raise ValueError("missing/duplicate testcase identity")
                records[identity] = ("fail" if case.find("failure") is not None else
                                     "skip" if case.find("skipped") is not None else "pass")
            if (process.returncode == 1) != any(v == "fail" for v in records.values()):
                raise ValueError("JUnit/exit mismatch")
            environment_digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps({
                "PYTHONHASHSEED":env.get("PYTHONHASHSEED"),"TZ":env.get("TZ"),
                "order":ordered},sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
            observations.append({"run_id":run_id, "factor_value":value, "records":records,
                                 "argv":argv, "exit":process.returncode, "report":str(report),
                                 "environment_digest":environment_digest})
        for relative, digest in source.items():
            if hashlib.sha256((root / relative).read_bytes()).hexdigest() != digest:
                raise ValueError("source changed during experiment")
        identities = set(observations[0]["records"])
        if any(set(obs["records"]) != identities for obs in observations):
            raise ValueError("collection drift")
        transitions, factors, findings = [], [], []
        for identity in sorted(identities):
            outcomes = [obs["records"][identity] for obs in observations]
            test_id = "::".join(identity)
            transitions.extend({"test_id":test_id,"run_id":obs["run_id"],"outcome":outcome,
                                "factor_value":obs["factor_value"],"seed":seed,
                                "environment_digest":obs["environment_digest"]}
                               for obs,outcome in zip(observations,outcomes))
            if diagnose_factor is not None:
                groups = {value:{outcome for state,outcome in zip(schedule,outcomes) if state == value}
                          for value in set(schedule)}
                aligned = sorted(map(tuple, map(sorted, groups.values()))) == [("fail",),("pass",)]
                factors.append({"test_id":test_id,"factor":diagnose_factor,
                    "status":"candidate_only" if aligned else "inconclusive",
                    "groups":{key:sorted(values) for key,values in groups.items()}})
            elif "pass" in outcomes and "fail" in outcomes:
                findings.append({"path":str(root),"line":None,"rule":"flaky-transition",
                    "severity":"warn","message":test_id + ": pass/fail transition"})
        deterministic = [identity for identity in identities
                         if all(obs["records"][identity] == "fail" for obs in observations)]
        heal_candidates = []
        for identity in sorted(identities):
            passed = [obs["run_id"] for obs in observations if obs["records"][identity] == "pass"]
            failed = [obs["run_id"] for obs in observations if obs["records"][identity] == "fail"]
            if passed and failed:
                heal_candidates.append({"test_id":"::".join(identity),
                    "pass_run_ids":passed,"fail_run_ids":failed})
        return ToolResult(tool="flaky", engine="pytest", engine_version=None,
            status="fail" if deterministic else "warn" if findings or factors else "ok",
            duration_ms=max(0,round((time.monotonic()-started)*1000)),
            summary=f"{len(identities)} tests across {len(schedule)} attempts",
            findings=findings, raw=None, artifacts=[obs["report"] for obs in observations],
            metadata={"source_digest":source_digest,"transitions":transitions,
                      "factor_experiment":factors,"evidence_source":"executed-attempts",
                      "deterministic_failures":["::".join(i) for i in deterministic],
                      "heal_candidates":heal_candidates})
    except (ContainmentError, OSError, ValueError, TypeError, ElementTree.ParseError,
            subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
        return error_result("flaky", "pytest", f"experiment incomplete: {type(exc).__name__}")
~~~

~~~python
# Add to src/rush/tools/flaky.py; existing ToolResult, Finding, ElementTree,
# error_result, elapsed_ms and now_ms imports remain available.
def analyze_imported_junit(report: Path, *, root: Path, permissions=None) -> ToolResult:
    from ..io.physical_paths import PhysicalRoot, ContainmentError
    start = now_ms()
    try:
        relative = report.relative_to(root) if report.is_absolute() else report
        checked = PhysicalRoot(root).open_contained(relative, purpose="read")
        document = ElementTree.parse(checked)
    except (ContainmentError, ValueError, OSError, ElementTree.ParseError) as exc:
        return error_result("flaky", "junit-report",
            f"imported report rejected: {type(exc).__name__}", duration_ms=elapsed_ms(start))
    rows = {}
    for suite in document.iter("testsuite"):
        for case in suite.findall("testcase"):
            classname, name = case.get("classname", ""), case.get("name", "")
            if not name:
                return error_result("flaky", "junit-report", "testcase name absent")
            run_id = case.get("rush_run_id") or suite.get("rush_run_id")
            environment = (case.get("rush_environment_digest")
                           or suite.get("rush_environment_digest"))
            outcome = ("error" if case.find("error") is not None else
                       "fail" if case.find("failure") is not None else
                       "skip" if case.find("skipped") is not None else "pass")
            identity = classname + "::" + name
            rows.setdefault(identity, []).append({"run_id":run_id,
                "environment_digest":environment,"outcome":outcome})
    if not rows:
        return error_result("flaky", "junit-report", "zero testcases")
    transitions, findings, deterministic = [], [], []
    for identity, attempts in sorted(rows.items()):
        complete = (all(item["run_id"] and item["environment_digest"] for item in attempts)
            and len({item["run_id"] for item in attempts}) == len(attempts)
            and len({item["environment_digest"] for item in attempts}) == 1)
        outcomes = {item["outcome"] for item in attempts}
        if not complete or "error" in outcomes or "skip" in outcomes:
            classification = "repeated_unresolved"
        elif outcomes == {"pass", "fail"}:
            classification = "flaky_transition"
            findings.append({"path":str(checked),"line":None,"rule":"flaky-transition",
                "severity":"warn","message":identity+": pass/fail across distinct runs"})
        elif outcomes == {"fail"}:
            classification = "deterministic_failure"
            deterministic.append(identity)
        else:
            classification = "repeated_not_flaky"
        transitions.append({"test_id":identity,"outcomes":[x["outcome"] for x in attempts],
            "run_ids":[x["run_id"] for x in attempts],"classification":classification})
    return ToolResult(tool="flaky",engine="junit-report",engine_version=None,
        status="fail" if deterministic else "warn" if findings else "ok",
        duration_ms=elapsed_ms(start),summary=f"{len(rows)} imported testcase identities",
        findings=findings,raw=None,artifacts=[str(checked)],
        metadata={"evidence_source":"imported-local-report","report_format":"junit",
            "transitions":transitions,"deterministic_failures":deterministic})
~~~

~~~python
# src/rush/tools/fuzz.py:369-455 — replace result/report decision after
# fresh Atheris process. Shared catalog CLI callback patch in §6 forwards
# --harness/--corpus/--seed/--max-runs/--timeout-seconds to existing __call__.
def fuzz_decision(iterations, crash_files, *, timed_out, exit_code):
    if crash_files: return "fail", "crash_observed"
    if timed_out: return "error", "timeout"
    if exit_code: return "error", "runner_failed"
    if iterations == 0: return "skipped", "zero_iterations"
    return "ok", "completed"
def fuzz_report_payload(seed, max_runs, harness_rel, corpus_rel, iterations,
                        crash_files, *, timed_out, argv, run_id,
                        harness_sha256, corpus_sha256, source_sha256):
    metrics = {"crashes":len(crash_files),"timeouts":int(timed_out),
               "iterations":iterations}
    return {"seed":seed,"max_runs":max_runs,"harness":harness_rel,
            "corpus":corpus_rel,"metrics":metrics,
            "crashes":metrics["crashes"],"timeouts":metrics["timeouts"],
            "argv":list(argv),"run_id":run_id,
            "harness_sha256":harness_sha256,"corpus_sha256":corpus_sha256,
            "source_sha256":source_sha256}
# Write payload with existing AtomicFile before registering report. Importer
# currently requires TOP-LEVEL crashes/timeouts/seed; nested metrics alone
# fails its own schema. Use decision before zero-iteration early return.

# src/rush/tools/fuzz.py:327-337 staged import support, before subprocess.
# Existing PhysicalRoot validates input containment. Copy pyproject and
# configured local package roots into isolated run; invoke sys.executable in
# already selected project environment with PYTHONPATH=run_root/src:run_root.
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
def stage_fuzz_imports(root, run_root, package_roots):
    root, run_root = Path(root).resolve(), Path(run_root).resolve()
    copied = []
    for relative in ["pyproject.toml", *package_roots]:
        rel = Path(relative)
        if rel.is_absolute() or ".." in rel.parts: raise ValueError("package_root_outside")
        source = (root / rel).resolve(strict=True)
        if not source.is_relative_to(root): raise ValueError("package_root_outside")
        destination = run_root / rel
        destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if source.is_dir(): shutil.copytree(source, destination, symlinks=False, dirs_exist_ok=True)
        else: shutil.copy2(source, destination)
        copied.append(rel.as_posix())
    return copied
~~~

~~~python
# src/rush/tools/fuzz.py::FuzzTool.run
from hashlib import sha256
from pathlib import Path
def registered_replay_argv(root, record, harness_rel, seed, python_binary):
    root = Path(root).resolve(strict=True)
    crash = (root / record["relative_path"]).resolve(strict=True)
    if not crash.is_relative_to(root) or not crash.is_file():
        raise ValueError("foreign_reproducer")
    if sha256(crash.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != record["sha256"]:
        raise ValueError("reproducer_digest_drift")
    harness = (root / harness_rel).resolve(strict=True)
    if not harness.is_relative_to(root) or not harness.is_file() or harness.suffix != ".py":
        raise ValueError("invalid_harness")
    if type(seed) is not int or seed < 0: raise ValueError("invalid_seed")
    return [python_binary, str(harness), str(crash), f"-seed={seed}", "-runs=1"]
~~~

## Command 28/79 — `rush_continuity` (W01)

**Use/function:** Save/list/restore session checkpoints, pack/retrieve context, inspect coordination/recovery and resume through explicit providers. Save requires cache-write. Restore returns checkpoint/context data, not a working-tree rollback; corrupt and missing checkpoints differ. Sources: `tools/continuity.py:194,260,372,485`.

**Routes/output:** Top-level `rush continuity` exposes generic inputs, but dedicated `rush session` and `rush context` routes expose useful operations; MCP has operation/name/files/goal/handle/provider inputs. Canonical result preserves execution and recovery metadata. It is a direct memory/context integration.

**Issue/path:** `run()` uses `path.resolve()` without logical-root normalization. Registered custom MCP pack therefore retains erroneous nested-file parent ownership (X08). Generic top-level help does not reveal full operation reachability. A successful provider process is not receiver consumption.

**Repair — exact path and data flow:** Change `SessionContinuityTool.run()` at `tools/continuity.py:152` to retain an invocation anchor and selected target separately. For `save/list/restore/provider_resume`, `path` is the caller's project anchor; make it absolute with lexical normalization against the invocation cwd, then call existing `resolve_logical_root()` (`invocation/targets.py:25`). For `context_pack`, first anchor `context_path` against that original invocation directory when relative, or preserve its absolute spelling; only then discover the logical root from the anchor or explicitly selected absolute target. Pass the uncollapsed target to `resolve_target(root, target, capability="read")` (`invocation/targets.py:116`) before deriving `relative_path`. Never call `resolve()` on an unvalidated target: an external symlink must not become a legitimate new root. For an explicitly supplied project root, require target containment there; it wins over ancestor-marker discovery. Return structured `error` on ambiguity/escape and `skipped` on a genuinely missing file. Root selection determines cache/journal ownership; it must not widen the set of files packed.

**Command-specific expansion — executable task replay, proposed:** Beyond checkpoint delivery, `resume_task` restores a task's unfinished behavior obligations, executes their approved checks against current source, and dispatches the bounded W21 repair operation for a reproduced failure. A saved command is historical data; current invocation must supply execution grants and confirm its verification contract. `continuity.py:SessionContinuityTool.run` dispatches to a new `_resume_task`; `continuity/receipts.py:save_receipt` retains obligation IDs/source hashes; existing `MemoryTool.plan_checks` orders checks; `PatchApplyTool` verifies any returned candidate. The new artifact is a replay result containing completed obligations, failed witnesses, proposed patch references and residual obligations—not another transcript. Default save/restore behavior does not execute anything. CLI proposal: `rush session resume-task NAME --request '<JSON>'`; MCP uses `operation="resume_task"`.

```json
{"before":{"operation":"restore","result":"checkpoint content"},"after":{"operation":"resume_task","name":"fix-invoice","request":{"required_checks":["invoice-total","negative-quantity"],"source_revision":"resolved HEAD","max_repairs":1},"artifact":{"kind":"task_replay","completed":["invoice-total"],"failed":["negative-quantity"],"next_operation":"repair_regression","residual":["negative-quantity"],"task_complete":false}}}
```

Add `_replay_disposition(required_ids, observed_outcomes)` in `tools/continuity.py`; keep every required ID, classify only actual current-source outcomes, and schedule repair only for observed assertion failures. Standalone proposed core (current-source receipt validation precedes this function):

```python
def _replay_disposition(required_ids, observed_outcomes):
    required = list(dict.fromkeys(required_ids))
    completed = [i for i in required if observed_outcomes.get(i) == "passed"]
    return {"completed": completed,
            "repair_checks": [i for i in required if observed_outcomes.get(i) == "assertion_failed"],
            "residual": [i for i in required if i not in completed],
            "task_complete": bool(required) and len(completed) == len(required)}

assert _replay_disposition(["total", "negative", "rounding"],
    {"total": "passed", "negative": "assertion_failed"}) == {
    "completed": ["total"], "repair_checks": ["negative"],
    "residual": ["negative", "rounding"], "task_complete": False}
assert _replay_disposition([], {})["task_complete"] is False
```

**Proposed operation wiring and acceptance (W01):** `SessionContinuityTool.run(operation="resume_task")` first calls its corrected `restore` using the caller's registered root, verifies checkpoint identity/freshness, and resolves every declared obligation to `{id,source_hashes,verification:{argv,cwd,expected_checks}}`. It invokes W13's isolated verifier/receipt path for every obligation against current bytes; only actual `passed` receipts enter `_replay_disposition`. `assertion_failed` receipts may enter W21 `repair_regression` only with separate worker grants and `max_repairs>0`; transport exit alone never marks them passed. CLI `rush session resume-task NAME --request '<JSON>'` and MCP `operation="resume_task"` forward the same request to this method; no second restore logic. Proposed fixture runs a saved `value=2` check that passes, changes source to `value=3`, then expects `freshness=stale`, one failed/residual obligation, zero `task_complete`, and unchanged working files. A provider that exits zero without a receiver check receipt still yields `transport_completed`, never `application_verified`. The pure `_replay_disposition` assertion above proves only classification; this fixture verifies actual replay.

Proposed replacement body at `src/rush/tools/continuity.py:SessionContinuityTool._resume_task`, dispatched from `run` only for `operation="resume_task"`; `run_check_plan` is fully defined at W13 and uses W18's OCI provider. Saved check plans are immutable by digest; caller must confirm the exact digest under current grants. `max_repairs=0` replays without model work.

```python
def _resume_task(self, started, root, name, request, granted):
    import hashlib
    import json
    from rush.invocation.targets import resolve_target
    from rush.patch.verifier import run_check_plan
    from rush.permissions import ExecutionPermissions, check_permissions
    from rush.tools.offline_runner import OfflineReviewTool

    allowed, missing = check_permissions(
        ExecutionPermissions(slow=True, build=True, artifact_write=True), granted)
    if not allowed:
        return self._result(started, "skipped", "Missing: " + ", ".join(missing),
                            operation="resume_task", granted=granted)
    restored = self._run_restore(started, root, name, granted)
    if restored["status"] != "ok":
        return restored
    handoff = restored["raw"]["metadata"]["handoff"]
    obligations = handoff.get("evidence_obligations", [])
    if not obligations or not isinstance(request, dict):
        return self._result(started, "error", "No replay obligations/request",
                            operation="resume_task", granted=granted)
    if (request.get("max_repairs", 0) not in (0, 1)
            or set(request.get("plans", {})) != {ob["id"] for ob in obligations}):
        return self._result(started, "error", "Replay plan IDs differ",
                            operation="resume_task", granted=granted)
    outcomes, receipts, stale = {}, {}, []
    for ob in obligations:
        check_id = ob["id"]
        plan = request["plans"][check_id]
        digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(plan, sort_keys=True,
            separators=(",", ":")).encode()).hexdigest()
        if digest != ob["required_check_sha256"] or plan["expected_checks"] != [check_id]:
            return self._result(started, "error", "Unapproved replay plan",
                                operation="resume_task", granted=granted)
        for rel, old_hash in ob["source_hashes"].items():
            if resolve_target(root, rel, capability="read").content_hash != old_hash:
                stale.append(rel)
        actual = run_check_plan(root, plan)
        outcomes[check_id] = actual["checks"][check_id]
        receipts[check_id] = actual["receipt_sha256"]
    replay = _replay_disposition([ob["id"] for ob in obligations], outcomes)
    worker = None
    if replay["repair_checks"] and request.get("max_repairs") == 1:
        job = request["repair_job"]
        if job["failure_receipt"]["check_id"] not in replay["repair_checks"]:
            raise ValueError("repair job is not bound to reproduced failure")
        worker = OfflineReviewTool().run(root, operation="repair_regression",
                                         request=job, permissions=granted)
    replay.update(receipt_sha256=receipts, changed_sources=sorted(set(stale)),
                  freshness="stale" if stale else "current", worker=worker,
                  application_verified=replay["task_complete"] and not stale)
    return self._result(started, "ok" if replay["task_complete"] else "warn",
                        "Current obligations replayed", operation="resume_task",
                        granted=granted, raw=replay)
```

Rewrite `value.py` to `VALUE=3`; invoke again, expecting `completed=[]`, `repair_checks=["value-is-two"]`, `changed_sources=["value.py"]`, `task_complete=false`, `application_verified=false` and source still `VALUE=3`. The test requires explicit `RUSH_TEST_OCI_RUNTIME` and `RUSH_TEST_OCI_IMAGE` local prerequisites and is **unexecuted**; it exercises verifier execution rather than supplied outcome strings.

```python
def test_resume_task_replays_current_source(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    import hashlib, json, os
    from pathlib import Path
    from rush.permissions import ExecutionPermissions
    from rush.tools.continuity import SessionContinuityTool

    runtime = os.environ["RUSH_TEST_OCI_RUNTIME"]
    image = os.environ["RUSH_TEST_OCI_IMAGE"]  # locally present name@sha256:<64 hex>
    root = tmp_path / "repo"
    root.mkdir()
    (root / ".git").mkdir()
    source = root / "value.py"
    source.write_text("VALUE = 2\n")
    (root / "check.py").write_text(
        "import json, os, runpy, sys\n"
        "ok = runpy.run_path('/work/value.py')['VALUE'] == 2\n"
        "open(os.environ['RUSH_CHECK_RECEIPT'], 'w').write(json.dumps("
        "{'schema_version':1,'checks':[{'id':'value-is-two',"
        "'outcome':'passed' if ok else 'assertion_failed'}]}))\n"
        "sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)\n")
    plan = {"argv": ["/work/check.py"], "cwd": ".", "timeout_s": 10,
            "expected_checks": ["value-is-two"],
            "runtime": {"runtime_path": runtime, "image_ref": image,
                        "entrypoint": "/usr/local/bin/python"}}
    digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(plan, sort_keys=True,
        separators=(",", ":")).encode()).hexdigest()
    obligation = {"id": "value-is-two", "source_hashes": {"value.py": hashlib.sha256(
        source.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}, "required_check_sha256": digest}
    tool = SessionContinuityTool()
    saved = tool.run(root, operation="save", name="value-task",
        handoff={"evidence_obligations": [obligation]},
        permissions=ExecutionPermissions(cache_write=True))
    assert saved["status"] == "ok"
    request = {"plans": {"value-is-two": plan}, "max_repairs": 0}
    grants = ExecutionPermissions(slow=True, build=True, artifact_write=True)
    first = tool.run(root, operation="resume_task", name="value-task",
                     request=request, permissions=grants)["raw"]
    assert first["completed"] == ["value-is-two"]
    assert len(first["receipt_sha256"]["value-is-two"]) == 64
    assert first["task_complete"] is True
    source.write_text("VALUE = 3\n")
    second = tool.run(root, operation="resume_task", name="value-task",
                      request=request, permissions=grants)["raw"]
    assert second["repair_checks"] == ["value-is-two"]
    assert second["changed_sources"] == ["value.py"]
    assert second["task_complete"] is False
    assert second["application_verified"] is False
    assert source.read_text() == "VALUE = 3\n"
```

**Proposed public replay and checkpoint forwarding (`src/rush/tools/continuity.py`, `src/rush/continuity/receipts.py`):** Put `_validated_obligations` below in `continuity/receipts.py` and import it with existing `save_receipt,restore_receipt` in `tools/continuity.py`; this avoids circular imports. Existing `SessionOperation` and `VALID_OPERATIONS` must both include `resume_task`. Existing public callable exposes only cache/network grants; replay additionally needs build/slow/artifact-write and must pass them through its existing `ExecutionPermissions` construction. `request` is the same structured JSON object for CLI `--request '<JSON>'` and MCP. Save is not allowed to drop obligations before replay.

```python
from typing import NotRequired, TypedDict

class ReplayRequest(TypedDict):
    plans: dict[str, dict]
    max_repairs: NotRequired[int]
    repair_job: NotRequired[dict]

def _validated_obligations(rows):
    import re
    if not isinstance(rows, list) or not rows or len(rows) > 32:
        raise ValueError("bounded evidence obligations required")
    ids = set()
    for row in rows:
        if (not isinstance(row, dict) or not isinstance(row.get("id"), str)
                or not row["id"] or row["id"] in ids
                or not isinstance(row.get("source_hashes"), dict)
                or not row["source_hashes"]
                or not all(isinstance(path, str) and path and isinstance(digest, str)
                           and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", digest)
                           for path, digest in row["source_hashes"].items())
                or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", row.get("required_check_sha256", ""))):
            raise ValueError("invalid checkpoint obligation")
        ids.add(row["id"])
    return rows
```

## Command 29/79 — `rush_memory` (W02)

**Use/function:** Durable SQLite/WAL typed artifacts, source allowlists, trust/ownership, revisions, compact retrieval, expansion, relations, maintenance, intent/recipes/check planning and handoff. CLI provides a rich dedicated group; MCP exposes corresponding payload operations. This is central context infrastructure, not universal host-native memory synchronization.

**Reproduced defects:** Legacy read-only `ask` initializes `.rush/memory.db` without cache-write. Expired artifact remains visible through legacy ask while compact ask excludes it. Archived artifact's current version expands with `OK` because expansion does not apply the same visibility predicate. Sources: `tools/memory.py:535`, `memory/store.py:610,2181`, `memory/retrieval.py:578`.

**Verified correction:** Current edit path demotes STATED to DERIVED and clears signature while preserving versions (`store.py:1109–1128`). Older report's contrary claim is obsolete.

**Repair:** In `MemoryTool._query()` (`tools/memory.py:535`), replace unconditional `TypedArtifactStore(root)` with the existing `open_readonly()` branch (`memory/store.py:1439`): absent DB returns empty results with `store_available=false`; old schema returns `skipped`/`migration_required`; neither initializes directories, WAL or migrations. Add this exact adapter in `src/rush/memory/store.py`; it reuses the existing `open_readonly()` connection, bypasses write-initializing `__init__`, and leaves connection ownership with the handler. `recall()` needs only `hash_content()` from `_merkle`; constructing `MerkleInvalidator` is forbidden here because its `__init__` creates `.rush/cache`. The read-only hash adapter preserves that computation with stdlib SHA-256 and no filesystem state. `search()` and `get_current()` additionally require only `_connect`, `_owner_scope_default`, and `project_root`. SQLite `mode=ro` rejects accidental mutation.

```python
class _ReadOnlyContentHasher:
    @staticmethod
    def hash_content(content):
        return hashlib.sha256(content.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


@classmethod
def from_readonly(cls, project_root, connection):
    if connection is None:
        raise ValueError("read-only connection required")
    store = cls.__new__(cls)
    store.project_root = Path(project_root).resolve()
    store.db_path = store.project_root / ".rush" / "memory.db"
    store._owner_scope_default = legacy_owner_scope(store.project_root)
    store._merkle = _ReadOnlyContentHasher()
    store._readonly_connection = connection
    return store

# First branch in existing TypedArtifactStore._connect().
if getattr(self, "_readonly_connection", None) is not None:
    return self._readonly_connection
```

```python
def test_existing_store_readonly_recall_creates_no_cache_or_db_write(tmp_path):
    import hashlib
    import shutil
    import time
    from rush.memory.store import MemoryArtifact, TypedArtifactStore

    writer = TypedArtifactStore(tmp_path)
    stored = writer.write(MemoryArtifact(
        id="readonly-fixture", family="memory", subject="domain_knowledge",
        trust_tier="EXTERNAL_WRITE", content={"note": "readonly needle"},
        source="fixture", created_at=time.time(),
    ))
    shutil.rmtree(tmp_path / ".rush" / "cache")
    database = tmp_path / ".rush" / "memory.db"
    before_inventory = sorted(str(path.relative_to(tmp_path))
                              for path in tmp_path.rglob("*"))
    before_database = hashlib.sha256(database.read_bytes()).hexdigest()

    opened = TypedArtifactStore.open_readonly(tmp_path)
    assert opened.available and opened.connection is not None
    reader = TypedArtifactStore.from_readonly(tmp_path, opened.connection)
    try:
        assert reader.get_current(stored.id).id == stored.id
        assert [row.id for row in reader.recall(
            "domain_knowledge", "readonly needle", ["fixture"]
        )] == [stored.id]
    finally:
        opened.connection.close()

    assert sorted(str(path.relative_to(tmp_path))
                  for path in tmp_path.rglob("*")) == before_inventory
    assert hashlib.sha256(database.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == before_database
    assert not (tmp_path / ".rush" / "cache").exists()
```

**Proposed operation wiring and acceptance (W02):** `MemoryTool.run(operation="recipe", request={"action":"learn",...})` resolves exact-version episode references through corrected visibility/owner filters, then **replays each training patch** and a disjoint held-out patch through W13's actual exact-check verifier. Existing `MemoryTool.write(source_kind="local_tool")` stores `EXTERNAL_WRITE`, not `DERIVED`; no code may claim it promoted a learned transformation by assertion. Keep the lower trust tier and explicit verified-run receipt hashes. Repetition or a caller-supplied `verifier_receipt_ref` alone grants no authority. Concrete proposed derivation and replay at `src/rush/memory/recipes.py:learn_verified_replacement`; add `action="learn"` to `MemoryTool._recipe` dispatch, but keep existing `record/resolve/outcome` unchanged. The caller resolves exact episode versions through corrected visibility-gated Memory API and passes their immutable content to this body. Each content record carries `base_commit`, exact before/after source hashes and W13 verification plan; `_replay_training_episode` below independently reexecutes it from the recorded Git commit, so even a forged old receipt cannot admit a recipe. Held-out verification then uses W13's proposed `PatchApplyTool.run(verification=...)`. This is all proposed product code; current production lacks that argument and route.

```python
def _replay_training_episode(root, episode, permissions):
    import difflib, hashlib, tempfile
    from pathlib import Path
    from rush.io.physical_paths import PhysicalRoot
    from rush.patch.applier import PatchApplier
    from rush.patch.verifier import run_check_plan
    from rush.runtime.subprocesses import run_subprocess
    if not permissions.build or not permissions.slow or not permissions.artifact_write:
        raise ValueError("training replay requires build, slow and artifact-write")
    before, after, rel = episode["before_source"], episode["after_source"], episode["path"]
    if (hashlib.sha256(before.encode()).hexdigest() != episode["before_sha256"]
            or hashlib.sha256(after.encode()).hexdigest() != episode["after_sha256"]):
        raise ValueError("episode source hash mismatch")
    patch = "".join(difflib.unified_diff(before.splitlines(keepends=True),
        after.splitlines(keepends=True), fromfile="a/" + rel, tofile="b/" + rel))
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rush-recipe-training-") as directory:
        checkout = Path(directory) / "source"
        clone = run_subprocess(["git", "clone", "--local", "--no-hardlinks", str(root),
                                str(checkout)], cwd=root, timeout=60)
        if clone.returncode != 0:
            raise ValueError("training source checkout unavailable")
        detached = run_subprocess(["git", "-C", str(checkout), "checkout", "--detach",
            episode["base_commit"]], cwd=root, timeout=30)
        if detached.returncode != 0:
            raise ValueError("training commit unavailable")
        target = PhysicalRoot(checkout).open_contained(rel, purpose="read")
        if target.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != before:
            raise ValueError("training commit source differs")
        baseline = run_check_plan(checkout, episode["verification"])
        if baseline["outcome"] != "behavior_failed":
            raise ValueError("training failure not reproduced")
        applied, message = PatchApplier.apply_patch_to_dir(checkout, patch)
        if not applied or target.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != after:
            raise ValueError("training patch failed: " + message)
        receipt = run_check_plan(checkout, episode["verification"])
        if receipt["outcome"] != "verified":
            raise ValueError("training verifier failed")
        return {"before": baseline, "after": receipt}
```

```python
def learn_verified_replacement(root, recipe_id, episodes, heldout, verification, permissions):
    import difflib, hashlib
    from rush.io.physical_paths import PhysicalRoot
    from rush.patch_generator import patch_target_paths
    from rush.runtime.filesystem import atomic_write_bytes
    from rush.tools.patch_apply import PatchApplyTool
    from rush.tools.memory import MemoryTool
    if len(episodes) < 2 or len({e["id"] for e in episodes}) != len(episodes):
        raise ValueError("two distinct verified episodes required")
    if len({e["intent"] for e in episodes}) != 1 or heldout["id"] in {e["id"] for e in episodes}:
        raise ValueError("intent or held-out identity mismatch")
    if not permissions.cache_write or not permissions.artifact_write:
        raise ValueError("learning requires cache-write and artifact-write")
    spans = []
    training_receipts = []
    for episode in episodes:
        before, after = episode["before_source"], episode["after_source"]
        training_receipts.append(_replay_training_episode(root, episode, permissions))
        changed = [op for op in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, before, after).get_opcodes()
                   if op[0] != "equal"]
        if len(changed) != 1:
            raise ValueError("one stable replacement required")
        _, i, j, k, m = changed[0]
        spans.append((before[i:j], after[k:m]))
    if len(set(spans)) != 1 or not spans[0][0]:
        raise ValueError("episodes do not teach one replacement")
    old, new = spans[0]
    source = heldout["source"]
    if source.count(old) != 1:
        raise ValueError("held-out source lacks unique precondition")
    rel = heldout["path"]
    target = PhysicalRoot(root).open_contained(rel, purpose="read")
    if target.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != source:
        raise ValueError("held-out source differs from pinned checkout")
    modified = source.replace(old, new, 1)
    patch = "".join(difflib.unified_diff(source.splitlines(keepends=True),
        modified.splitlines(keepends=True), fromfile="a/" + rel, tofile="b/" + rel))
    if patch_target_paths(patch) != (rel,):
        raise ValueError("learned patch target invalid")
    patch_hash = hashlib.sha256(patch.encode()).hexdigest()
    patch_path = atomic_write_bytes(root, ".rush/learn/" + patch_hash + ".patch", patch.encode())
    result = PatchApplyTool().run(root, patch_file=patch_path, dry_run=True,
                                  verification=verification, permissions=permissions)
    receipt = result.get("metadata", {}).get("verification_receipt")
    if result["status"] != "ok" or result["metadata"].get("verified") is not True or not receipt:
        return {"state": "rejected_replay", "patch_sha256": patch_hash}
    stored = MemoryTool().run(root, operation="write", subject="domain_knowledge",
        content={"kind": "learned_replacement", "recipe_id": recipe_id,
                 "intent": episodes[0]["intent"],
                 "old": old, "new": new, "patch_sha256": patch_hash,
                 "training_ids": [e["id"] for e in episodes],
                 "training_receipts": [{"before": r["before"]["receipt_sha256"],
                                        "after": r["after"]["receipt_sha256"]}
                                       for r in training_receipts],
                 "heldout_id": heldout["id"], "heldout_receipt": receipt,
                 "checks": verification["expected_checks"],
                 "required_symbol": heldout["required_symbol"],
                 "dependency_path": heldout["dependency_path"],
                 "dependency_digest": hashlib.sha256(PhysicalRoot(root).open_contained(
                     heldout["dependency_path"], purpose="read").read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                 "config_path": heldout["config_path"],
                 "config_digest": hashlib.sha256(PhysicalRoot(root).open_contained(
                     heldout["config_path"], purpose="read").read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                 "owner_scope": heldout["owner_scope"]},
        source="worker:recipe", source_kind="local_tool",
        owner_scope=heldout["owner_scope"], permissions=permissions)
    if stored["status"] != "ok":
        return {"state": "verified_but_not_stored", "receipt": receipt}
    return {"state": "eligible_for_admission", "patch_sha256": patch_hash,
            "receipt": receipt, "store": stored}
```

```python
def _load_recipe_episode(self, root, ref, owner_scope, session_allowlist):
    import base64, json
    from rush.memory.store import OwnerScope, TypedArtifactStore
    if (not isinstance(ref, dict) or not isinstance(ref.get("id"), str)
            or not isinstance(ref.get("episode_id"), str) or not ref["episode_id"]
            or not isinstance(ref.get("version"), int) or isinstance(ref["version"], bool)
            or not session_allowlist):
        raise ValueError("exact visible episode reference required")
    owner = OwnerScope.from_value(owner_scope)
    row = TypedArtifactStore(root).get_current(ref["id"])
    if (row is None or row.artifact_version != ref["version"]
            or row.owner_scope != owner or row.source not in session_allowlist):
        raise ValueError("episode version, owner or visibility mismatch")
    chunks, offset = [], 0
    for _ in range(16):
        page = self.run(root, operation="expand", session_allowlist=session_allowlist,
            request={"id": ref["id"], "version": ref["version"], "offset": offset,
                     "max_bytes": 8192, "max_tokens": 2048, "encoding": "base64"})
        raw = page["raw"]
        if raw["code"] != "OK":
            raise ValueError("episode is no longer expandable")
        data = raw["data"]
        if data["id"] != ref["id"] or data["version"] != ref["version"] or data["offset"] != offset:
            raise ValueError("episode page identity changed")
        chunks.append(base64.b64decode(data["content_base64"], validate=True))
        if sum(map(len, chunks)) > 65536:
            raise ValueError("episode exceeds bounded content")
        if data["complete"]:
            content = json.loads(b"".join(chunks).decode("utf-8"))
            if not isinstance(content, dict) or content.get("id") != ref["episode_id"]:
                raise ValueError("episode content identity mismatch")
            return content
        next_offset = data["next_offset"]
        if not isinstance(next_offset, int) or next_offset <= offset:
            raise ValueError("episode page did not advance")
        offset = next_offset
    raise ValueError("episode requires too many pages")

def _learn_recipe(self, started, root, granted, request, session_allowlist):
    from rush.permissions import ExecutionPermissions, check_permissions
    from rush.runtime.isolated_process import IsolationUnavailable
    from rush.memory.recipes import learn_verified_replacement
    required = ExecutionPermissions(cache_write=True, artifact_write=True, build=True, slow=True)
    allowed, missing = check_permissions(required, granted)
    if not allowed:
        return self._envelope_result(started, "recipe", "E_PERMISSION",
                                     {"message": "Missing grants: " + ", ".join(missing)})
    refs = request.get("episode_refs")
    if (not isinstance(refs, list) or not 2 <= len(refs) <= 8
            or not isinstance(request.get("heldout_ref"), dict)
            or not isinstance(request.get("verification"), dict)
            or not request.get("owner_scope")):
        return self._envelope_result(started, "recipe", "E_INPUT",
                                     {"message": "bounded recipe learning request required"})
    try:
        episodes = [self._load_recipe_episode(root, ref, request["owner_scope"],
                    session_allowlist) for ref in refs]
        heldout = self._load_recipe_episode(root, request["heldout_ref"],
                    request["owner_scope"], session_allowlist)
        result = learn_verified_replacement(root, request["recipe_id"], episodes,
            heldout, request["verification"], granted)
    except IsolationUnavailable:
        return self._envelope_result(started, "recipe", "E_UNAVAILABLE",
                                     {"message": "pinned process isolation unavailable"})
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        return self._envelope_result(started, "recipe", "E_INPUT", {"message": str(exc)})
    return self._envelope_result(started, "recipe",
        "OK" if result["state"] == "eligible_for_admission" else "UNRESOLVED", result)
```

```python
def test_recipe_learn_public_route(tmp_path):
    import hashlib, json, os, subprocess
    from pathlib import Path
    import pytest
    from rush.memory.store import TypedArtifactStore
    from rush.permissions import ExecutionPermissions
    from rush.tools.memory import MemoryTool

    image, runtime = os.getenv("RUSH_TEST_OCI_IMAGE"), os.getenv("RUSH_TEST_OCI_RUNTIME")
    if not image or not runtime:
        pytest.skip("approved pinned local OCI verifier required")
    root = tmp_path.resolve()
    def git(*args):
        return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=root, check=True,
                              capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    git("init")
    before = "def add_one(x):\n    return x + 0\n"
    after = "def add_one(x):\n    return x + 1\n"
    for name in ("case1.py", "case2.py", "heldout.py"):
        (root / name).write_text(before)
    (root / "config.json").write_text("{}\n")
    (root / "check.py").write_text(
        "import json,runpy,sys\n"
        "from pathlib import Path\n"
        "f=runpy.run_path('/work/'+sys.argv[1])['add_one']\n"
        "ok=f(2)==3 and f(-1)==0\n"
        "Path('/out/checks.json').write_text(json.dumps({'schema_version':1,"
        "'checks':[{'id':'add-one','outcome':'passed' if ok else 'assertion_failed'}]}))\n"
        "sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)\n")
    git("add", "case1.py", "case2.py", "heldout.py", "config.json", "check.py")
    git("-c", "user.name=Fixture", "-c", "user.email=fixture@example.invalid",
        "commit", "-m", "base fixture")
    base1 = git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
    (root / "note.txt").write_text("second training revision\n")
    git("add", "note.txt")
    git("-c", "user.name=Fixture", "-c", "user.email=fixture@example.invalid",
        "commit", "-m", "second revision")
    base2 = git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
    def plan(name):
        return {"argv": ["/work/check.py", name], "cwd": ".", "timeout_s": 10,
                "expected_checks": ["add-one"], "runtime": {
                    "runtime_path": runtime, "image_ref": image,
                    "entrypoint": "/usr/local/bin/python"}}
    owner = {"kind": "project", "id": str(root)}
    tool = MemoryTool()
    refs = []
    for episode_id, name, commit in (("training-1", "case1.py", base1),
                                      ("training-2", "case2.py", base2)):
        content = {"id": episode_id, "intent": "add-one", "path": name,
            "before_source": before, "after_source": after,
            "before_sha256": hashlib.sha256(before.encode()).hexdigest(),
            "after_sha256": hashlib.sha256(after.encode()).hexdigest(),
            "base_commit": commit, "verification": plan(name)}
        written = tool.run(root, operation="write", subject="domain_knowledge",
            content=content, source="worker:recipe", source_kind="local_tool",
            owner_scope=owner, permissions=ExecutionPermissions(cache_write=True))
        assert written["status"] == "ok"
        refs.append({"id": written["raw"]["id"],
                     "version": written["raw"]["artifact_version"],
                     "episode_id": episode_id})
    held = {"id": "held-out", "source": before, "path": "heldout.py",
        "required_symbol": "add_one", "dependency_path": "check.py",
        "config_path": "config.json", "owner_scope": owner}
    written = tool.run(root, operation="write", subject="domain_knowledge",
        content=held, source="worker:recipe", source_kind="local_tool",
        owner_scope=owner, permissions=ExecutionPermissions(cache_write=True))
    assert written["status"] == "ok"
    held_ref = {"id": written["raw"]["id"],
                "version": written["raw"]["artifact_version"],
                "episode_id": "held-out"}
    request = {"action": "learn", "recipe_id": "fix-1", "episode_refs": refs,
               "heldout_ref": held_ref, "verification": plan("heldout.py"),
               "owner_scope": owner}
    result = tool(root, operation="recipe", request=request,
        session_allowlist=["worker:recipe"], allow_cache_write=True,
        allow_artifact_write=True, allow_build=True, allow_slow=True)
    assert result["raw"]["code"] == "OK"
    learned = result["raw"]["data"]
    assert learned["state"] == "eligible_for_admission"
    assert len(learned["receipt"]) == 64
    row = TypedArtifactStore(root).get_current(learned["store"]["raw"]["id"])
    assert row is not None and row.content["training_ids"] == ["training-1", "training-2"]
    assert len(row.content["training_receipts"]) == 2
    assert all(len(pair["before"]) == len(pair["after"]) == 64
               for pair in row.content["training_receipts"])
    assert str(getattr(row.trust_tier, "value", row.trust_tier)) == "EXTERNAL_WRITE"
    bad = {**request, "episode_refs": [{**refs[0], "version": refs[0]["version"] + 1}, refs[1]]}
    rejected = tool(root, operation="recipe", request=bad,
        session_allowlist=["worker:recipe"], allow_cache_write=True,
        allow_artifact_write=True, allow_build=True, allow_slow=True)
    assert rejected["raw"]["code"] == "E_INPUT"
```

```python
def _load_semantic_snapshot(root, relative):
    import json
    from rush.io.physical_paths import PhysicalRoot

    path = PhysicalRoot(root).open_contained(relative, purpose="read")
    if not path.is_file() or path.stat().st_size > 1_048_576:
        raise ValueError("semantic snapshot must be an ordinary file at most 1 MiB")
    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    nodes = data.get("nodes") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
    if data.get("schema_version") != 1 or not isinstance(nodes, list) or len(nodes) > 10_000:
        raise ValueError("invalid semantic snapshot schema")
    indexed = {}
    for node in nodes:
        if (not isinstance(node, dict) or set(node) !=
                {"id", "role", "name", "state", "relationships"}
                or not all(isinstance(node[key], str) for key in ("id", "role", "name"))
                or not node["id"] or not isinstance(node["state"], dict)
                or not isinstance(node["relationships"], dict) or node["id"] in indexed):
            raise ValueError("invalid or duplicate semantic node")
        indexed[node["id"]] = node
    return indexed


def _compare_semantic_snapshots(self, root, baseline_path, candidate_path, started, permissions):
    from rush.permissions import build_execution_metadata
    from rush.tools.base import ToolResult
    from rush.tools.common import elapsed_ms

    before = _load_semantic_snapshot(root, baseline_path)
    after = _load_semantic_snapshot(root, candidate_path)
    findings = []
    fields = ("role", "name", "state", "relationships")
    for node_id in sorted(set(before) | set(after)):
        if node_id not in after:
            findings.append({"path": candidate_path, "line": 1,
                "rule": "semantic-drift/removed-control", "severity": "error",
                "message": f"semantic node {node_id!r} was removed",
                "evidence": {"node_id": node_id, "before": before[node_id], "after": None}})
            continue
        if node_id not in before:
            findings.append({"path": candidate_path, "line": 1,
                "rule": "semantic-drift/added-control", "severity": "warn",
                "message": f"semantic node {node_id!r} was added",
                "evidence": {"node_id": node_id, "before": None, "after": after[node_id]}})
            continue
        for field in fields:
            if before[node_id][field] != after[node_id][field]:
                findings.append({"path": candidate_path, "line": 1,
                    "rule": f"semantic-drift/{field}-changed", "severity": "error",
                    "message": f"semantic node {node_id!r} changed {field}",
                    "evidence": {"node_id": node_id, "before": before[node_id][field],
                                 "after": after[node_id][field]}})
    return ToolResult(tool=self.name, engine="semantic-snapshot", engine_version="1",
        status="fail" if findings else "ok", duration_ms=elapsed_ms(started),
        summary=f"semantic-drift: {len(findings)} snapshot difference(s)",
        findings=findings, raw={"coverage": {"baseline_nodes": len(before),
            "candidate_nodes": len(after), "complete": True}},
        metadata={"execution": build_execution_metadata(
            "executed", granted=permissions, producer="semantic-snapshot")})

# At top of SemanticDriftTool.run after started/permissions initialization.
if mode == "compare":
    if baseline_path is None or candidate_path is None:
        raise ValueError("baseline_path and candidate_path required for compare")
    return _compare_semantic_snapshots(
        self, path, baseline_path, candidate_path, started, permissions
    )
if mode != "tagged_tests":
    raise ValueError(f"unknown semantic drift mode: {mode}")
```

```python
def _common_postconditions(traces):
    if len(traces) < 2 or any(t["passed"] is not True for t in traces):
        return {}
    if len({t["task"] for t in traces}) != 1:
        return {}
    return {key: value for key, value in traces[0]["state"].items()
            if all(key in t["state"] and t["state"][key] == value for t in traces[1:])}

traces = [{"task": "save", "passed": True, "state": {"dirty": False}, "label": "Save"},
          {"task": "save", "passed": True, "state": {"dirty": False}, "label": "Save draft"}]
assert _common_postconditions(traces) == {"dirty": False}
assert _common_postconditions([traces[0]]) == {}
```
