```javascript
const fs = require('node:fs');
const http = require('node:http');
const path = require('node:path');
const crypto = require('node:crypto');
const { chromium } = require('playwright');
const root = fs.realpathSync('/work');
const inside = target => target === root || target.startsWith(root + path.sep);
const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
  let target;
  try {
    const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://127.0.0.1');
    target = path.resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname));
    if (!inside(target)) { res.writeHead(403); res.end(); return; }
    target = fs.realpathSync(target);
    if (!inside(target)) { res.writeHead(403); res.end(); return; }
    if (fs.statSync(target).isDirectory()) target = fs.realpathSync(path.join(target, 'index.html'));
    if (!inside(target)) { res.writeHead(403); res.end(); return; }
    const ext = path.extname(target);
    const type = ({'.html':'text/html','.js':'text/javascript','.css':'text/css',
                   '.png':'image/png','.webp':'image/webp',
                   '.svg':'image/svg+xml'})[ext] || 'application/octet-stream';
    res.writeHead(200, {'content-type':type});
    fs.createReadStream(target).pipe(res);
  } catch (_) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); }
});
(async () => {
  const scenarios = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('/out/scenarios.json', 'utf8'));
  await new Promise(resolve => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', resolve));
  const base = 'http://127.0.0.1:' + server.address().port;
  const browser = await chromium.launch({headless:true});
  const out = {};
  try {
    for (const item of scenarios) {
      const page = await browser.newPage({viewport:{width:item.width,height:item.height}});
      const requests = [], responses = [];
      page.on('response', r => responses.push(r));
      page.on('requestfailed', r => requests.push({url:new URL(r.url()).pathname,status:0}));
      await page.goto(base + item.path, {waitUntil:'networkidle'});
      if (item.toggle) {
        await page.getByRole('button', {name:item.toggle}).click();
        await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
      }
      for (const r of responses) {
        let bytes = null;
        try { bytes = (await r.body()).length; } catch (_) {}
        requests.push({url:new URL(r.url()).pathname,status:r.status(),bytes});
      }
      const state = await page.evaluate(() => window.__RUSH_TASK_STATE__ ?? null);
      const images = await page.locator('img').evaluateAll(nodes => nodes.map(n => ({
        currentSrc:new URL(n.currentSrc).pathname,naturalWidth:n.naturalWidth,
        naturalHeight:n.naturalHeight,renderedWidth:n.getBoundingClientRect().width})));
      const screenshot = await page.screenshot();
      out[item.id] = {requests,render_passed:await page.locator('body').isVisible(),
        state,images,html:(await page.locator('body').innerHTML()).slice(0,8192),
        screenshot_sha256:crypto.createHash('sha256').update(screenshot).digest('hex')};
      await page.close();
    }
  } finally { await browser.close(); server.close(); }
  fs.writeFileSync('/out/browser.json', JSON.stringify(out));
})().catch(e => { console.error(e.message); server.close(); process.exitCode = 1; });
```

```python
def run_browser_scenarios(root, scenarios, *, runtime_path, image_ref, timeout_s):
    import hashlib, json, tempfile
    from pathlib import Path
    from rush.io.physical_paths import PhysicalRoot
    from rush.runtime.isolated_process import run_isolated_argv

    if not isinstance(scenarios, list) or not 1 <= len(scenarios) <= 16:
        raise ValueError("one to sixteen browser scenarios required")
    ids = []
    for item in scenarios:
        if not isinstance(item, dict) or not isinstance(item.get("id"), str) or not item["id"]:
            raise ValueError("scenario ID required")
        page = item.get("path")
        if (not isinstance(page, str) or not page.startswith("/") or ".." in Path(page).parts
                or any(c in page for c in "?%#\\\n\r")):
            raise ValueError("contained scenario path required")
        if any(type(item.get(k)) is not int or not 1 <= item[k] <= 4096
               for k in ("width", "height")):
            raise ValueError("bounded viewport required")
        ids.append(item["id"])
    if len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
        raise ValueError("duplicate scenario ID")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rush-browser-") as temporary:
        scratch = Path(temporary)
        script = Path(__file__).with_name("browser_probe.cjs").read_bytes()
        (scratch / "browser_probe.cjs").write_bytes(script)
        (scratch / "scenarios.json").write_text(json.dumps(scenarios), encoding="utf-8")
        proc = run_isolated_argv(root, scratch, runtime_path=runtime_path,
            image_ref=image_ref, entrypoint="/usr/local/bin/node",
            argv=["/out/browser_probe.cjs"], timeout_s=timeout_s)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise ValueError("browser scenario execution failed")
        path = PhysicalRoot(scratch).open_contained("browser.json", purpose="read")
        if not path.is_file() or path.stat().st_size > 1024 * 1024:
            raise ValueError("browser receipt missing or oversized")
        raw = path.read_bytes()
        evidence = json.loads(raw)
        if not isinstance(evidence, dict) or set(evidence) != set(ids):
            raise ValueError("browser scenario coverage incomplete")
        return {"scenarios": evidence, "receipt_sha256": hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()}
```

`pyproject.toml` wheel already packages `src/rush`; add `browser_probe.cjs` under `src/rush/runtime/` and verify built wheel contains it. This is proposed packaging verification, not an assertion that Playwright or Chromium is installed. Browser image requires local approved Node/Playwright/Chromium and fails `isolation_unavailable` before page execution if absent.

Concrete proposed `src/rush/tools/dead_asset.py:DeadAssetTool._prove_removal` consumes that browser adapter. Existing `PatchSandboxManager` requires clean Git source, so a dirty source returns explicit `source_not_frozen`; it never silently judges older HEAD. Each candidate is handled independently and no original asset is removed:

```python
def _prove_removal(self, root, candidates, scenarios, required_scenarios, runtime):
    import hashlib
    from rush.io.physical_paths import PhysicalRoot
    from rush.patch.sandbox import PatchSandboxManager
    from rush.runtime.browser_probe import run_browser_scenarios

    required = list(required_scenarios)
    if not required or len(required) != len(set(required)):
        raise ValueError("nonempty unique scenario IDs required")
    submitted = {item["id"] for item in scenarios}
    if submitted != set(required):
        return [{"candidate": item["path"], "state": "incomplete",
                 "missing": sorted(set(required) - submitted)} for item in candidates]
    baseline = run_browser_scenarios(root, scenarios, **runtime)
    results = []
    for item in candidates:
        rel, expected = item["path"], item["sha256"]
        source = PhysicalRoot(root).open_contained(rel, purpose="read")
        if not source.is_file() or hashlib.sha256(source.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != expected:
            raise ValueError("asset changed before removal trial")
        manager = PatchSandboxManager(root)
        checkout = manager.create_sandbox()
        try:
            target = PhysicalRoot(checkout).open_contained(rel, purpose="write")
            if hashlib.sha256(target.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != expected:
                raise ValueError("sandbox asset differs from frozen source")
            target.unlink()
            after = run_browser_scenarios(checkout, scenarios, **runtime)
            normalized = {}
            for sid in required:
                before_requests = baseline["scenarios"][sid]["requests"]
                after_requests = after["scenarios"][sid]["requests"]
                before_ok = {r["url"] for r in before_requests if r["status"] == 200}
                missing = [r["url"] for r in after_requests
                           if r["url"] in before_ok and (r["status"] == 0 or r["status"] >= 400)]
                normalized[sid] = {"missing_requests": sorted(set(missing)),
                                   "render_passed": after["scenarios"][sid]["render_passed"]}
            decision = _assess_asset_removal(normalized, required)
            results.append({"candidate": rel, **decision,
                "baseline_receipt": baseline["receipt_sha256"],
                "candidate_receipt": after["receipt_sha256"]})
        finally:
            manager.cleanup_sandbox(checkout)
    return results
```

```python
def _classify_claim_challenge(base_outcome, candidate_outcome):
    if base_outcome != "passed":
        return "invalid_or_preexisting_challenge"
    if candidate_outcome == "assertion_failed":
        return "contradicted"
    if candidate_outcome == "passed":
        return "not_refuted_by_this_check"
    return "incomplete"

assert _classify_claim_challenge("passed", "assertion_failed") == "contradicted"
assert _classify_claim_challenge("assertion_failed", "assertion_failed") == "invalid_or_preexisting_challenge"
assert _classify_claim_challenge("passed", "passed") == "not_refuted_by_this_check"
assert _classify_claim_challenge("passed", "infrastructure_error") == "incomplete"
```

**Proposed executable route (`tools/pr_synthesize.py:PrSynthesizeTool._challenge_claim`):** Parse claimed behavior into explicit test patch, expected check ID and base/candidate refs. Validate test patch changes only declared test files with W21 `_validate_candidate_scope`; apply it to two fresh `PatchSandboxManager` checkouts pinned to base and candidate commits. Run identical W13 `run_check_plan` in W18 isolated process for both; require exact check ID, base `passed`, candidate `assertion_failed` before `_classify_claim_challenge` yields `contradicted`. Treat import/timeout/zero collection on either side as `incomplete`, retain both receipt hashes, test patch hash and source revisions in PR card. No PR publication. Proposed core:

```python
def _challenge_claim_check(base_checkout, candidate_checkout, test_patch, test_rel, plan):
    import hashlib
    from rush.patch.applier import PatchApplier
    from rush.patch.verifier import run_check_plan
    from rush.tools.offline_runner import OfflineReviewTool
    for checkout in (base_checkout, candidate_checkout):
        OfflineReviewTool()._validate_candidate_scope(checkout, test_patch, [test_rel])
        applied, message = PatchApplier.apply_patch_to_dir(checkout, test_patch)
        if not applied:
            raise ValueError(message)
    before = run_check_plan(base_checkout, plan)
    after = run_check_plan(candidate_checkout, plan)
    check_id = plan["expected_checks"][0]
    return {"claim_state": _classify_claim_challenge(before["checks"][check_id],
            after["checks"][check_id]), "base_receipt": before["receipt_sha256"],
            "candidate_receipt": after["receipt_sha256"],
            "test_patch_sha256": hashlib.sha256(test_patch.encode()).hexdigest()}
```

Caller creates/cleans both owned checkouts in `try/finally`, verifies commit/tree hashes and CODEOWNERS/base permission before invoking this body. Fixture `parse('é')` passes on base, candidate ASCII guard raises assertion failure; exact output `claim_state=contradicted` with two nonempty receipt hashes. A test patch importing nonexistent module must give `incomplete`, not `contradicted`. Pinned OCI and Git fixture acceptance unexecuted.

Add named `operation: str="synthesize", request: dict|None=None, allow_build: bool=False, allow_slow: bool=False` to `__call__`, construct the existing permission object with build/slow as well as artifact-write, and pass it to `run(path,operation=operation,request=request,permissions=permissions)`. Add these named arguments to `run`, dispatch before current PR prose generation, and expose `--request '<JSON>'` through the shared typed CLI. `request` is the following concrete schema; `test_rel` must be inside declared test files and `verification.expected_checks` must contain exactly one check for this first claim challenge. W21's existing proposed local-model method produces the test diff; the existing `_challenge_claim_check` body above executes that diff against both commits.

```python
# Typed request target: src/rush/tools/pr_synthesize.py
from typing import TypedDict

class ClaimChallengeRequest(TypedDict):
    schema_version: int
    claim_id: str
    claim_text: str
    base_commit: str
    candidate_commit: str
    test_rel: str
    verification: dict
    model_runtime: dict
    max_attempts: int

# At top of PrSynthesizeTool.run, before existing card assembly.
if operation == "challenge_claims":
    if request is None:
        raise ValueError("claim challenge request required")
    return self._challenge_claims(path, request, permissions)
if operation != "synthesize":
    raise ValueError(f"unknown pr_synthesize operation: {operation}")

def _challenge_claims(self, root, request, permissions):
    import hashlib, json, re, tempfile
    from pathlib import Path
    from rush.runtime.subprocesses import run_subprocess
    from rush.tools.offline_runner import OfflineReviewTool
    started = now_ms()  # existing pr_synthesize.py import
    if not all((permissions.build, permissions.slow, permissions.artifact_write)):
        return skipped_result(self.name, "builtin", "build, slow and artifact-write grants required")
    required = set(ClaimChallengeRequest.__annotations__)
    if (set(request) != required or request["schema_version"] != 1
            or type(request["max_attempts"]) is not int
            or not 1 <= request["max_attempts"] <= 3):
        raise ValueError("invalid claim challenge request")
    for key in ("base_commit", "candidate_commit"):
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", request[key]):
            raise ValueError("commit SHA required")
    check_plan = request["verification"]
    if len(check_plan.get("expected_checks", [])) != 1:
        raise ValueError("one exact challenge check required")
    # Verify both immutable commits belong to the selected project before model work.
    for key in ("base_commit", "candidate_commit"):
        proof = run_subprocess(["git", "cat-file", "-t", request[key]], cwd=root, timeout=10)
        if proof.returncode != 0 or proof.stdout.strip() != "commit":
            raise ValueError("challenge commit unavailable")
    model = OfflineReviewTool()
    prompt = json.dumps({"schema_version": 1, "instruction":
        "Return JSON with schema_version=1 and one unified-diff test_patch that would refute this claim; modify only test_rel.",
        "claim_id": request["claim_id"], "claim_text": request["claim_text"],
        "base_commit": request["base_commit"],
        "candidate_commit": request["candidate_commit"],
        "test_rel": request["test_rel"]}, sort_keys=True)
    attempts = []
    for _ in range(request["max_attempts"]):
        completion = model._invoke_local_model(prompt, request["model_runtime"],
            root, timeout_seconds=120)
        response = json.loads(completion)
        if response.get("schema_version") != 1 or not isinstance(response.get("test_patch"), str):
            raise ValueError("invalid challenge model response")
        patch = response["test_patch"]
        model._validate_candidate_scope(root, patch, [request["test_rel"]])
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rush-claim-challenge-") as temporary:
            checkouts = []
            for arm in ("base_commit", "candidate_commit"):
                checkout = Path(temporary) / arm
                cloned = run_subprocess(["git", "clone", "--local", "--no-hardlinks",
                    str(root), str(checkout)], cwd=root, timeout=60)
                if cloned.returncode:
                    raise ValueError("claim challenge checkout failed")
                selected = run_subprocess(["git", "checkout", "--detach", request[arm]],
                    cwd=checkout, timeout=30)
                if selected.returncode:
                    raise ValueError("claim challenge ref changed")
                head = run_subprocess(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=checkout, timeout=10)
                if head.returncode or head.stdout.strip() != request[arm]:
                    raise ValueError("claim challenge checkout mismatch")
                checkouts.append(checkout)
            verdict = _challenge_claim_check(checkouts[0], checkouts[1], patch,
                request["test_rel"], check_plan)
        attempts.append(verdict)
        if verdict["claim_state"] in {"contradicted", "not_refuted_by_this_check"}:
            break
        prompt += "\nPrevious challenge incomplete: " + json.dumps(verdict, sort_keys=True)
    return ToolResult(tool=self.name, engine="local-model+isolated-checks",
        engine_version=None, status="fail" if attempts[-1]["claim_state"] == "contradicted" else "warn",
        duration_ms=elapsed_ms(started), summary="PR claim challenged against base and candidate",
        findings=[], raw={"claim_id": request["claim_id"],
            "claim_state": attempts[-1]["claim_state"],
            "base_commit": request["base_commit"],
            "candidate_commit": request["candidate_commit"], "attempts": attempts,
            "pr_published": False})
```

## Command 55/79 — `rush_ship_clean` (X01)


**Proposed code/contract artifact (not applied):**

```python
# src/rush/tools/ship/cleaner.py — proposed adapter after ScratchCleaner.clean.
# It consumes actual _result keys; clean() itself enforces artifact_write.
def cleaner_result(detail, *, duration_ms):
    status = detail["status"]
    if status == "skipped":
        canonical = "skipped"
    elif status == "error" or detail["refused_count"]:
        canonical = "error"
    elif status in {"preview", "ok"}:
        canonical = "ok"
    else:
        canonical = "error"  # Unknown/partial cleanup cannot pass.
    return {"tool": "ship_clean", "engine": "rush", "engine_version": None,
            "status": canonical, "duration_ms": duration_ms,
            "summary": f"{detail['removed_count']} removed; {detail['refused_count']} refused",
            "findings": [{"message": path, "rule_id": "CLEAN-REFUSED"}
                         for path in detail["refused_items"]], "raw": detail}
# MCP returns this object; CLI --json emits it, while text CLI reads same result.
```

**Proposed domain check (unexecuted):** Apply adapter above, then run `rtk proxy uv run --python 3.12 python -` with following fixture. It invokes existing `ScratchCleaner` on registered files and verifies denial, deletion, refusal, and unchanged refused bytes. Named CLI/MCP regression below remains proposed.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from time import perf_counter
from rush.permissions import ExecutionPermissions
from rush.tools.ship.cleaner import ScratchCleaner, register_owned_artifact
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    root = Path(d); a = root / ".rush/runs/R/a.txt"; b = root / ".rush/runs/R/b.txt"
    a.parent.mkdir(parents=True); a.write_text("A"); b.write_text("B")
    grant = ExecutionPermissions(artifact_write=True)
    register_owned_artifact(root, a, "test", grant, run_id="R")
    register_owned_artifact(root, b, "test", grant, run_id="R")
    b.write_text("changed")
    start=perf_counter(); detail=ScratchCleaner(root).clean(apply=True)
    denied = cleaner_result(detail,duration_ms=(perf_counter()-start)*1000)
    assert denied["status"] == "skipped" and a.exists()
    start=perf_counter(); detail=ScratchCleaner(root).clean(apply=True, permissions=grant)
    result = cleaner_result(detail,duration_ms=(perf_counter()-start)*1000)
    assert result["status"] == "error" and result["raw"]["removed_items"] == [".rush/runs/R/a.txt"]
    assert result["raw"]["refused_items"] == [".rush/runs/R/b.txt"]
    assert not a.exists() and b.read_text() == "changed"
```

Add the migration and every current producer call site; malformed v1 rows fail before `AtomicFile.write_json`:

```python
# cleaner.py
def migrate_cleanup_registry_v1(root, permissions):
    allowed, missing = check_permissions(
        ExecutionPermissions(artifact_write=True), permissions)
    if not allowed:
        raise PermissionError(f"registry migration requires {', '.join(missing)}")
    physical = PhysicalRoot(root)
    registry = physical.open_contained(REGISTRY_PATH, purpose="read")
    if not stat.S_ISREG(os.lstat(registry).st_mode):
        raise CleanupRegistryError("cleanup registry is not an ordinary file")
    try:
        raw = json.loads(registry.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, UnicodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        raise CleanupRegistryError(f"cleanup registry is malformed: {exc}") from exc
    if (not isinstance(raw, dict) or set(raw) != {"version", "artifacts"}
            or type(raw["version"]) is not int or raw["version"] != 1
            or not isinstance(raw["artifacts"], list)):
        raise CleanupRegistryError("cleanup registry is not migratable v1")
    migrated = []
    for old in raw["artifacts"]:
        valid = _validate_registry_entry(old, version=1)
        parts = Path(valid["path"]).parts
        if len(parts) < 4 or parts[:2] != RUNS_PREFIX:
            raise CleanupRegistryError("v1 row has no exact run identity")
        migrated.append(_validate_registry_entry({**valid, "run_id": parts[2]}))
    migrated.sort(key=lambda item: item["path"])
    if len({item["path"] for item in migrated}) != len(migrated):
        raise CleanupRegistryError("cleanup registry contains duplicate paths")
    AtomicFile(physical).write_json(REGISTRY_PATH,
        SanitizedJsonValue.from_value({"version": 2, "artifacts": migrated}))
    return {"migrated": len(migrated), "version": 2}
```

```python
import json
from rush.permissions import ExecutionPermissions
from rush.tools.ship.cleaner import ScratchCleaner, register_owned_artifact

def test_ship_clean_run_id_persisted_and_forwarded(tmp_path):
    grant = ExecutionPermissions(artifact_write=True)
    a, b = tmp_path/".rush/runs/A/a", tmp_path/".rush/runs/B/b"
    for target in (a, b):
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        target.write_text(target.name, encoding="utf-8")
    register_owned_artifact(tmp_path, a, "test", grant, run_id="A")
    register_owned_artifact(tmp_path, b, "test", grant, run_id="B")
    result = ScratchCleaner(tmp_path).clean(apply=True, permissions=grant, run_id="A")
    assert result["removed_items"] == [".rush/runs/A/a"]
    assert not a.exists() and b.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "b"
    raw = json.loads((tmp_path/".rush/cleanup.json").read_text())
    assert raw["version"] == 2 and len(raw["artifacts"]) == 1
    assert raw["artifacts"][0]["path"] == ".rush/runs/B/b"
    assert raw["artifacts"][0]["run_id"] == "B"

def test_migrate_cleanup_registry_v1_is_atomic(tmp_path):
    import hashlib
    import pytest
    from rush.tools.ship.cleaner import CleanupRegistryError, migrate_cleanup_registry_v1
    grant = ExecutionPermissions(artifact_write=True)
    artifact = tmp_path / ".rush/runs/A/a"
    artifact.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    artifact.write_bytes(b"A")
    stat = artifact.stat()
    registry = tmp_path / ".rush/cleanup.json"
    row = {"path": ".rush/runs/A/a", "sha256": hashlib.sha256(b"A").hexdigest(),
           "length": 1, "producer": "test", "device": stat.st_dev, "inode": stat.st_ino}
    registry.write_text(json.dumps({"version": 1, "artifacts": [row]}), encoding="utf-8")
    assert migrate_cleanup_registry_v1(tmp_path, grant) == {"migrated": 1, "version": 2}
    migrated = json.loads(registry.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert migrated["artifacts"][0]["run_id"] == "A"
    malformed = json.dumps({"version": 1, "artifacts": [{**row, "path": ".rush/runs/a"}]})
    registry.write_text(malformed, encoding="utf-8")
    before = registry.read_bytes()
    with pytest.raises(CleanupRegistryError, match="no exact run identity"):
        migrate_cleanup_registry_v1(tmp_path, grant)
    assert registry.read_bytes() == before
```

**New capability proposal — minimize retained artifacts while preserving an executable failure witness.** Beyond deleting registered files, let an agent ask which artifacts are actually necessary to reproduce a specific failure. Add `ScratchCleaner.minimize_reproducer(request, *, replay)` in `src/rush/tools/ship/cleaner.py`; expose `operation="minimize_reproducer"` on `mcp.py:rush_ship_clean` and `rush ship clean --request FILE`. Strict request fields: `schema_version=1`, `run_id`, `witness_id`, `artifact_ids`, `max_replays`, `apply=false`. Resolve witness to source/environment hashes, argv, fixture inputs and expected failure signature in existing run artifacts. No command inferred from failure text.

Start with full registered set; replay in existing isolated execution boundary. Remove one artifact from the sandbox copy, replay identical inputs, retain removal only if exact failure signature still occurs. Repeat until budget exhausted or every single deletion changes the witness. Result is **one-deletion-minimal for this replay**, not global minimum or proof for all environments. Missing files, runner errors and infrastructure failures cannot count as reproducing the target failure. Retain untested candidates. Persistent cleanup still passes original hash/inode/containment checks; changed witness/source blocks apply. Existing ownership protections stay mandatory.

Production replay must invoke recorded argv inside W18 isolation and compare exact observed failure signature; public-route acceptance below remains proposed. Run with `rtk proxy uv run --python 3.12 python -` after adding helper:

```python
def minimize_reproducer_artifacts(ids, *, witness_signature, max_replays, replay):
    retained = list(dict.fromkeys(ids)); runs = 0
    def reproduces(candidate):
        nonlocal runs
        runs += 1
        result = replay(candidate)
        return result["completed"] and result["signature"] == witness_signature
    def result(state):
        return {"retained":retained, "minimality":state, "replay_count":runs, "applied":False}
    if max_replays < 1: return result("budget_limited")
    if not reproduces(retained): return result("baseline_not_reproduced")
    while True:
        for artifact in tuple(retained):
            if runs == max_replays: return result("budget_limited")
            candidate = [x for x in retained if x != artifact]
            if reproduces(candidate):
                retained = candidate
                break  # Restart: earlier trials were against a different retained set.
        else:
            return result("one_deletion")  # Every deletion tested against FINAL set.
seen = []
def replay(ids):
    seen.append(tuple(ids))
    return {"completed": True, "signature": "W7" if "seed.json" in ids else "NO_FAILURE"}
r = minimize_reproducer_artifacts(
    ["seed.json", "failure.trace", "debug.log"], witness_signature="W7",
    max_replays=7, replay=replay)
assert r["retained"] == ["seed.json"] and r["minimality"] == "one_deletion"
assert len(seen) == 6 and r["applied"] is False
limited = minimize_reproducer_artifacts(["seed.json", "debug.log"],
    witness_signature="W7", max_replays=3, replay=replay)
assert limited["retained"] == ["seed.json"] and limited["minimality"] == "budget_limited"
```

**Proposed code/contract artifact (not applied):**

```python
# src/rush/tools/ship/env_linter.py — replace receiver-agnostic AST loop.
import ast
def scan_python_env(source, path):
    tree = ast.parse(source, filename=path)
    accesses, dynamic = [], []
    class Scan(ast.NodeVisitor):
        def __init__(self, aliases=None): self.aliases = dict(aliases or {})
        def kind(self, node):
            if isinstance(node, ast.Name): return self.aliases.get(node.id)
            if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and node.attr == "environ" and self.kind(node.value) == "os":
                return "environ"
            return None
        def record(self, key_node, node, required):
            key = key_node.value if isinstance(key_node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(key_node.value, str) else None
            row = {"key": key, "path": path, "line": node.lineno, "required": required}
            (accesses if key is not None else dynamic).append(row)
        def visit_Import(self, node):
            for alias in node.names:
                self.aliases[alias.asname or alias.name.split('.')[0]] = "os" if alias.name == "os" else None
        def visit_ImportFrom(self, node):
            for alias in node.names:
                self.aliases[alias.asname or alias.name] = alias.name if node.module == "os" and alias.name in {"getenv", "environ"} else None
        def visit_Call(self, node):
            f = node.func
            os_getenv = isinstance(f, ast.Attribute) and f.attr == "getenv" and self.kind(f.value) == "os"
            env_get = isinstance(f, ast.Attribute) and f.attr == "get" and self.kind(f.value) == "environ"
            direct = isinstance(f, ast.Name) and self.aliases.get(f.id) == "getenv"
            if os_getenv or env_get or direct:
                default = node.args[1] if len(node.args) > 1 else next((kw.value for kw in node.keywords if kw.arg == "default"), None)
                optional = isinstance(default, ast.Constant) and default.value is not None
                self.record(node.args[0] if node.args else ast.Constant(None), node, not optional)
            self.generic_visit(node)
        def visit_Subscript(self, node):
            if self.kind(node.value) == "environ": self.record(node.slice, node, True)
            self.generic_visit(node)
        def visit_Assign(self, node):
            self.visit(node.value)
            for target in node.targets:
                for child in ast.walk(target):
                    if isinstance(child, ast.Name): self.aliases[child.id] = None
        def visit_AnnAssign(self, node):
            if node.value: self.visit(node.value)
            if isinstance(node.target, ast.Name): self.aliases[node.target.id] = None
        def visit_FunctionDef(self, node):
            blocked = {a.arg for a in (*node.args.posonlyargs, *node.args.args, *node.args.kwonlyargs)}
            if node.args.vararg: blocked.add(node.args.vararg.arg)
            if node.args.kwarg: blocked.add(node.args.kwarg.arg)
            for stmt in node.body:
                if isinstance(stmt, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)):
                    blocked.add(stmt.name); continue
                blocked.update(n.id for n in ast.walk(stmt) if isinstance(n, ast.Name) and isinstance(n.ctx, ast.Store))
            nested = Scan({k:v for k,v in self.aliases.items() if k not in blocked})
            for stmt in node.body: nested.visit(stmt)
            self.aliases[node.name] = None
        visit_AsyncFunctionDef = visit_FunctionDef
        def visit_ClassDef(self, node):
            nested = Scan(self.aliases)
            for stmt in node.body: nested.visit(stmt)
            self.aliases[node.name] = None
    Scan().visit(tree)
    return accesses, dynamic
```

**Route and trigger:** `rush ship env`; after changing environment-dependent configuration or preparing deployment. Shared domain: `tools/ship/env_linter.py:8–53`; MCP `mcp.py:109–118`, CLI `cli.py:3986–4004`.

**Actual capability/output:** Parses Python, finds calls whose attribute name is `getenv` or `get`, compares first string argument with `.env.example`. MCP emits a short sentence; CLI lists missing declarations and exits nonzero.

**Reproduced defect:** `data.get("NOT_AN_ENV_VAR")` becomes an environment dependency; `os.environ["REAL_ENV_VAR"]` is missed. The scanner does not resolve call receiver/import aliases and skips parse failures. This creates both false warnings and false assurance.

**Concrete patch specification:** Replace attribute-name matching in `EnvParityLinter.lint` (`tools/ship/env_linter.py:14–53`) with import-bound AST matching. Build aliases for `import os as o`, `from os import getenv as g`, and `from os import environ as e`; recognize only resolved `os.getenv(KEY)`, `os.environ.get(KEY)` and `os.environ[KEY]`. Track rebinding within lexical scope so a later assignment to `o` invalidates its import alias. Read `.env.example` key names only. Return `accesses=[{key,path,line,required}]`, `missing`, `dynamic_accesses`, `parse_errors`, `files_examined`; `required=false` when an explicit non-None default is present. A nonliteral key produces a dynamic-access record, not a guessed key. Missing example produces `reason="missing_template"`, not zero dependencies. Both wrappers must retain these fields in `raw` and emit one finding per undeclared required key.

**Ordinary extension (not innovation):** Add `languages` to shared linter options and both public routes. # Additional code in src/rush/tools/ship/env_linter.py; scan_python_env above.
```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
from tree_sitter import Language, Parser
import tree_sitter_typescript
def scan_ts_env(source, path, *, tsx=False):
    data = source.encode('utf-8')
    grammar = tree_sitter_typescript.language_tsx() if tsx else tree_sitter_typescript.language_typescript()
    root = Parser(Language(grammar)).parse(data).root_node
    if root.has_error: raise SyntaxError(path)
    accesses, unsupported = [], []
    def text(node): return data[node.start_byte:node.end_byte].decode('utf-8')
    # Conservative: syntax-only scanner cannot prove process is global if locally bound.
    shadowed = any(n.type in {'variable_declarator', 'formal_parameter', 'import_specifier'}
                   and (n.child_by_field_name('name') is not None)
                   and text(n.child_by_field_name('name')) == 'process'
                   for n in walk(root))
    for node in walk(root):
        if node.type not in {'member_expression', 'subscript_expression'}: continue
        obj = node.child_by_field_name('object')
        if obj is None or text(obj) not in {'process.env', 'import.meta.env'}: continue
        if text(obj) == 'process.env' and shadowed:
            unsupported.append({'path':path,'line':node.start_point.row+1,'reason':'shadowed_process'})
            continue
        key_node = node.child_by_field_name('property' if node.type == 'member_expression' else 'index')
        if key_node is None: continue
        key = text(key_node) if node.type == 'member_expression' else None
        if node.type == 'subscript_expression' and key_node.type == 'string':
            try: key = json.loads(text(key_node))
            except json.JSONDecodeError: pass
        row = {'key':key,'path':path,'line':node.start_point.row+1,'required':True}
        (accesses if isinstance(key,str) else unsupported).append(row)
    return accesses, unsupported
def walk(node):
    yield node
    for child in node.named_children: yield from walk(child)

# Replace EnvParityLinter.lint body; same shared call for CLI and MCP.
def lint(self, *, languages=('python',), include_optional=False):
    suffixes = {'python':'.py','javascript':'.js','typescript':'.ts','tsx':'.tsx'}
    if not languages or any(lang not in suffixes for lang in languages): raise ValueError('unsupported_language')
    root = Path(self.project_root).resolve()
    accesses, dynamic, parse_errors, examined = [], [], [], []
    for lang in dict.fromkeys(languages):
        for path in sorted(root.rglob('*'+suffixes[lang])):
            if any(part in {'.git','.venv','node_modules','tests'} for part in path.relative_to(root).parts): continue
            rel = path.relative_to(root).as_posix(); examined.append(rel)
            try:
                source = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
                found, unknown = (scan_python_env(source,rel) if lang == 'python' else
                                  scan_ts_env(source,rel,tsx=lang == 'tsx'))
                accesses.extend(found); dynamic.extend(unknown)
            except (SyntaxError, UnicodeError, OSError, ImportError) as exc:
                parse_errors.append({'path':rel,'reason':type(exc).__name__})
    template = root / '.env.example'
    declared = {line.split('=',1)[0].strip() for line in template.read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines()
                if '=' in line and line.strip() and not line.lstrip().startswith('#')} if template.is_file() else set()
    missing = sorted({a['key'] for a in accesses if a['key'] not in declared and (a['required'] or include_optional)})
    return {'codebase_vars':sorted({a['key'] for a in accesses}), 'declared_vars':sorted(declared),
            'missing_in_example':missing, 'missing':missing, 'accesses':accesses,
            'dynamic_accesses':dynamic, 'parse_errors':parse_errors, 'files_examined':examined,
            'reason':'missing_template' if not template.is_file() else None,
            'passed':not missing and not dynamic and not parse_errors and template.is_file()}

# Replace src/rush/mcp.py::rush_ship_env body and typed signature.
def rush_ship_env(path: Path = Path('.'), languages: list[str] | None = None,
                  include_optional: bool = False) -> dict:
    return EnvParityLinter(path).lint(languages=languages or ('python',),
                                      include_optional=include_optional)

# Replace src/rush/cli.py::ship_env_cmd decorator/signature/body (retain group registration).
@ship_group.command(name='env')
@click.option('--language', 'languages', multiple=True,
              type=click.Choice(['python','javascript','typescript','tsx']))
@click.option('--include-optional', is_flag=True)
@click.option('--json', 'as_json', is_flag=True)
def ship_env_cmd(languages: tuple[str, ...], include_optional: bool, as_json: bool) -> None:
    res = EnvParityLinter().lint(languages=languages or ('python',),
                                 include_optional=include_optional)
    if as_json: click.echo(json.dumps(res, sort_keys=True))
    else: click.echo('Ship Env: ' + ('PASS' if res['passed'] else 'FAIL') +
                     f"; missing={res['missing']}; dynamic={len(res['dynamic_accesses'])}; parse_errors={len(res['parse_errors'])}")
    if not res['passed']: raise click.exceptions.Exit(1)
```

```python
from itertools import product
def experiment_environment(domains, *, execute, max_runs):
    if type(max_runs) is not int or max_runs < 0: raise ValueError("invalid_budget")
    keys = sorted(domains)
    values = [list(dict.fromkeys(domains[k])) for k in keys]
    if any(not v or any(x is not None and not isinstance(x, str) for x in v) for v in values):
        raise ValueError("invalid_domain")
    total = 1
    for v in values: total *= len(v)
    rows = []
    for combination in product(*values):
        if len(rows) == max_runs: break
        env = {k:v for k,v in zip(keys, combination) if v is not None}
        rows.append({"environment":env, "observed":execute(dict(env))})
    return {"runs":rows, "untested_combinations":total-len(rows)}
def execute(env):
    return {"retry_count": int(env.get("RETRY", "0")) if env["TLS_MODE"] == "on" else 0,
            "tls_enabled": env["TLS_MODE"] == "on"}
r = experiment_environment({"TLS_MODE": ["on", "off"], "RETRY": [None, "2"]},
                           execute=execute, max_runs=4)
assert len(r["runs"]) == 4 and r["untested_combinations"] == 0
bad = [x for x in r["runs"] if x["environment"] == {"TLS_MODE":"off", "RETRY":"2"}]
assert len(bad) == 1 and bad[0]["observed"]["retry_count"] == 0
```

**Proposed code/contract artifact (not applied):**

```python
# src/rush/tools/ship/cockpit.py — proposed replacements/additions.
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path
from time import perf_counter
import json, subprocess, tomllib
from packaging.version import Version
from rush.io.physical_paths import PhysicalRoot
from rush.tools.api_diff import ApiDiffer
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class VectorVerdict(BaseModel):
    name: str
    passed: bool
    duration_ms: float
    details: str
    state: str = 'passed'  # Existing five constructors remain valid; set failed below.
    findings: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)

class ShipGateVerdict(BaseModel):
    all_passed: bool
    score_pct: float
    vectors: list[VectorVerdict] = Field(default_factory=list)

def timed_vector(run):
    started = perf_counter()
    try: verdict = run()
    except Exception as exc:
        verdict = VectorVerdict(name=run.__name__, passed=False, state='incomplete',
                                duration_ms=0, details=type(exc).__name__)
    verdict.duration_ms = round((perf_counter()-started)*1000, 3)
    if verdict.state == 'passed' and not verdict.passed: verdict.state = 'failed'
    return verdict

def semver_vector(root, base_ref):
    root = Path(root)
    check = subprocess.run(['git','rev-parse','--verify',base_ref+'^{commit}'],cwd=root,
                           capture_output=True,text=True,check=False)
    if check.returncode: return VectorVerdict(name='semver',passed=False,state='incomplete',
                                               duration_ms=0,details='base_ref_unavailable')
    old = subprocess.run(['git','show',base_ref+':pyproject.toml'],cwd=root,
                         capture_output=True,text=True,check=False)
    if old.returncode: return VectorVerdict(name='semver',passed=False,state='incomplete',
                                             duration_ms=0,details='base_version_unavailable')
    previous = Version(tomllib.loads(old.stdout)['project']['version'])
    current = Version(tomllib.loads((root/'pyproject.toml').read_text())['project']['version'])
    delta = ApiDiffer(root).diff_public_api(base_ref=base_ref)
    breaks = delta['breaking_changes_count']
    passed = not breaks or current.major > previous.major
    return VectorVerdict(name='semver',passed=passed,state='passed' if passed else 'failed',
                         duration_ms=0,details=f'breaking={breaks}; {previous} -> {current}',
                         findings=[] if passed else ['ERR-SEMVER-BREAKING'])

def receipt_vector(root, required_receipts, source_sha256):
    physical = PhysicalRoot(root); missing=[]
    if not required_receipts or len(source_sha256) != 64:
        return VectorVerdict(name='gate',passed=False,state='incomplete',duration_ms=0,
                             details='release_receipts_or_source_missing')
    for ref in required_receipts:
        receipt_id, relative_path, expected_sha256 = ref['id'], ref['path'], ref['sha256']
        path = physical.open_contained(relative_path,purpose='read')
        if not path.resolve().as_posix().startswith((Path(root).resolve()/'.rush/runs').as_posix()+'/'):
            raise ValueError('receipt_outside_runs')
        try: data = path.read_bytes()
        except OSError:
            missing.append(receipt_id); continue
        import hashlib
        if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != expected_sha256:
            missing.append(receipt_id); continue
        row = json.loads(data)
        if row.get('receipt_id') != receipt_id or row.get('source_sha256') != source_sha256 or row.get('status') != 'passed':
            missing.append(receipt_id)
    return VectorVerdict(name='gate',passed=not missing,state='passed' if not missing else 'incomplete',
                         duration_ms=0,details='missing='+','.join(missing),findings=missing)

# Replace ShipCockpit.evaluate_gate body, retaining existing five run_* methods.
def evaluate_gate(self, *, base_ref, required_receipts, source_sha256):
    import re
    if not isinstance(base_ref, str) or not base_ref or base_ref.startswith("-"):
        raise ValueError("invalid base_ref")
    if not isinstance(source_sha256, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", source_sha256):
        raise ValueError("invalid source_sha256")
    if not isinstance(required_receipts, list):
        raise ValueError("required_receipts must be a list")
    receipt_ids = set()
    for ref in required_receipts:
        if (not isinstance(ref, dict) or set(ref) != {"id", "path", "sha256"}
                or not all(isinstance(ref[k], str) and ref[k] for k in ref)
                or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", ref["sha256"])
                or ref["id"] in receipt_ids):
            raise ValueError("invalid or duplicate receipt reference")
        receipt_ids.add(ref["id"])
    jobs = [self.run_clean_vector,self.run_env_vector,self.run_docs_vector,
            self.run_migration_vector,self.run_pack_vector,
            lambda:semver_vector(self.project_root,base_ref),
            lambda:receipt_vector(self.project_root,required_receipts,source_sha256)]
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=7) as executor:
        vectors = list(executor.map(timed_vector,jobs))
    passed = all(v.state == 'passed' for v in vectors)
    return ShipGateVerdict(all_passed=passed,score_pct=round(100*sum(v.passed for v in vectors)/7,1),
                           vectors=vectors)

def gate_result(project_root, *, base_ref, required_receipts, source_sha256):
    started = perf_counter()
    verdict = ShipCockpit(project_root).evaluate_gate(base_ref=base_ref,
        required_receipts=required_receipts, source_sha256=source_sha256)
    states = {v.state for v in verdict.vectors}
    status = "ok" if verdict.all_passed else "error" if "failed" in states else "skipped"
    return {"tool":"ship-gate", "engine":"builtin", "engine_version":None,
        "status":status, "duration_ms":round((perf_counter()-started)*1000, 3),
        "summary":"Ship gate passed" if verdict.all_passed else "Ship gate blocked",
        "findings":[{"path":str(project_root), "line":1, "rule":"ship."+v.name,
            "severity":"error" if v.state == "failed" else "warning", "message":v.details}
            for v in verdict.vectors if not v.passed], "raw":verdict.model_dump()}
```

**Actual capability:** Runs clean, env, docs, migration and package checks concurrently, computes percentage of passing vectors. **Reproduced: five vectors**, despite seven-vector description. Each vector's duration is a literal constant (5/10/12/8/6 ms). MCP collapses detailed verdicts to `Ship Gate PASSED/FAILED (N%)`.

**Concrete patch specification:** Replace `cockpit.py:VectorVerdict`/`ShipGateVerdict` and `ShipCockpit.evaluate_gate` with code above; add module-level `gate_result`. Existing five `run_*_vector` constructors remain valid; `timed_vector` overwrites their literal duration and maps failed `passed` to failed state. Proposed semver worker uses actual `ApiDiffer.diff_public_api(base_ref)`, whose live keys are `passed`, `breaking_changes_count`, `breaking_changes` (not a `status` key); X13 strengthens its signature detection. Validate Git base and base version before comparison. CLI and MCP both call `gate_result`, retaining every vector inside canonical ToolResult `raw`; failed checks return `error`, incomplete-only gates return `skipped`, and CLI exits nonzero for either.

**Exact specification blocker:** Phase 42 §3/FR-02-05 names seven vectors `clean, env, migration, semver, docs, pack, gate`; the seventh is named `gate`, also the aggregator's name. It does not define an independent seventh analysis here. Concrete proposed resolution: define seventh `gate` as verification-receipt validation, consuming declared test/security/API/package receipt IDs and rejecting missing, failed or source-mismatched receipts. It must not recursively call `evaluate_gate`. Ratify that meaning against ADR-0031/0046 before implementing the seventh worker; keep this obligation open, not silently replace seven with six.

```python
# src/rush/mcp.py — replace rush_ship_gate body/signature, retaining registration.
def rush_ship_gate(path: Path = Path('.'), base_ref: str = 'main',
                   required_receipts: list[dict[str,str]] | None = None,
                   source_sha256: str = '') -> dict:
    from rush.tools.ship.cockpit import gate_result

             required_receipts=required_receipts or [],source_sha256=source_sha256)

# src/rush/cli.py: replace ship_gate_cmd and its decorators.
@ship_group.command(name="gate")
@click.option("--base", "base_ref", default="main", show_default=True)
@click.option("--source-sha256", required=True)
@click.option("--receipt-ref", "receipt_refs", multiple=True, required=True)
def ship_gate_cmd(base_ref, source_sha256, receipt_refs):
    import json, re
    from rush.tools.ship.cockpit import gate_result
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", source_sha256):
        raise click.BadParameter("expected lowercase SHA-256", param_hint="--source-sha256")
    parsed = []
    for value in receipt_refs:
        try:
            ref = json.loads(value)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise click.BadParameter("invalid JSON", param_hint="--receipt-ref") from exc
        if (not isinstance(ref, dict) or set(ref) != {"id", "path", "sha256"}
                or not all(isinstance(ref[k], str) and ref[k] for k in ref)
                or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", ref["sha256"])):
            raise click.BadParameter("expected {id,path,sha256} with string values and SHA-256",
                                     param_hint="--receipt-ref")
        parsed.append(ref)
    result = gate_result(Path.cwd(),base_ref=base_ref,
        required_receipts=parsed, source_sha256=source_sha256)
    click.echo(json.dumps(result))
    if result["status"] != "ok":
        raise click.exceptions.Exit(1)
```

```python
def validate_workflow_replay(*, artifact_sha256, required, receipts):
    by_checkpoint = {}
    for receipt in receipts:
        key = receipt["checkpoint"]
        if key in by_checkpoint: raise ValueError("duplicate_checkpoint")
        if receipt["artifact_sha256"] != artifact_sha256 or not receipt["evidence_id"]:
            raise ValueError("unbound_receipt")
        by_checkpoint[key] = receipt
    missing = [k for k in required if k not in by_checkpoint]
    passed = all(by_checkpoint[k]["state"] == "passed" for k in required if k in by_checkpoint)
    return {"release_ready":bool(required) and not missing and passed, "not_reached":missing}
r = validate_workflow_replay(
    artifact_sha256="wheel-S", required=["discovery","grounding","edit","verification"],
    receipts=[{"checkpoint":"discovery","state":"passed","artifact_sha256":"wheel-S","evidence_id":"E1"},
              {"checkpoint":"grounding","state":"failed","artifact_sha256":"wheel-S","evidence_id":"E2"}])
assert r["release_ready"] is False
assert r["not_reached"] == ["edit", "verification"]
```

**Proposed code/contract artifact (not applied):**

```python
# src/rush/token_economy/ast_skeletonizer.py::AstSkeletonizer.skeletonize_python:
# replace `except Exception: return code` with `except SyntaxError: raise`.
# src/rush/token_economy/compressor.py::PythonAstOutlineCompressor.compress_source:
# apply the same parse-error rule; both CLI aliases currently use this class.
# src/rush/mcp.py::rush_token_outline and both CLI outline handlers call one
# shared `outline_file(path, focus_symbol)` in src/rush/token_economy/outline.py:
from pathlib import Path
import ast
import hashlib
def python_outline(source, focus_symbol=None):
    tree = ast.parse(source)
    definitions = []
    class Collect(ast.NodeVisitor):
        def __init__(self): self.stack = []
        def visit_ClassDef(self, node):
            self.stack.append(node.name); self.generic_visit(node); self.stack.pop()
        def visit_FunctionDef(self, node): self.function(node)
        def visit_AsyncFunctionDef(self, node): self.function(node)
        def function(self, node):
            qualified = ".".join([*self.stack, node.name])
            definitions.append((qualified, node))
            self.stack.append(node.name); self.generic_visit(node); self.stack.pop()
    Collect().visit(tree)
    wanted = focus_symbol.rsplit("::", 1)[-1] if focus_symbol else None
    matches = [(name, node) for name, node in definitions
               if name == wanted or name.endswith("." + str(wanted))]
    if wanted and len(matches) != 1:
        raise ValueError("ambiguous_or_missing_focus:" + ",".join(name for name, _ in definitions))
    focus = matches[0][1] if wanted else None
    class Skeleton(ast.NodeTransformer):
        def visit_FunctionDef(self, node): return self.function(node)
        def visit_AsyncFunctionDef(self, node): return self.function(node)
        def function(self, node):
            if node is focus:
                return node
            if focus is not None and any(descendant is focus for descendant in ast.walk(node)):
                return self.generic_visit(node)
            doc = node.body[0] if ast.get_docstring(node) else None
            node.body = ([doc] if doc else []) + [ast.Expr(value=ast.Constant(value=Ellipsis))]
            return node
    omitted_nodes = [(name, node) for name, node in definitions if node is not focus
                     and not (focus is not None and any(child is focus for child in ast.walk(node)))]
    source_lines = source.encode('utf-8').splitlines(keepends=True)
    def byte_offset(line, column): return sum(len(part) for part in source_lines[:line-1]) + column
    omitted = [(name, byte_offset(node.body[0].lineno,node.body[0].col_offset),
                byte_offset(node.end_lineno,node.end_col_offset)) for name,node in omitted_nodes]
    result = Skeleton().visit(tree)
    ast.fix_missing_locations(result)
    return ast.unparse(result), omitted, [name for name,_node in definitions]
def outline_file(path, focus_symbol=None, *, root=Path.cwd(), recoverable=False,
                 editable=False, permissions=None):
    from rush.io.physical_paths import PhysicalRoot
    from rush.token_economy.counter import FastBPETokenCounter
    root = Path(root).resolve(); supplied = Path(path)
    path = (supplied if supplied.is_absolute() else root / supplied).resolve()
    try: relative = path.relative_to(root)
    except ValueError: return {"status":"error","raw":{"reason":"path_outside_project"}}
    path = PhysicalRoot(root).open_contained(relative, purpose='read')
    if not path.is_file(): return {"status":"error","raw":{"reason":"file_not_found"}}
    if focus_symbol and '::' in focus_symbol:
        focus_path, _ = focus_symbol.rsplit('::',1)
        if focus_path != relative.as_posix():
            return {"status":"error","raw":{"reason":"focus_file_mismatch"}}
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    if suffix not in {".py", ".ts", ".tsx", ".rs"}:
        return {"status": "skipped", "raw": {"reason": "unsupported_language"}}
    source = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    try:
        if suffix == ".py":
            outline, omitted, names = python_outline(source, focus_symbol)
        else:
            outline, omitted = tree_sitter_outline(source, suffix, focus_symbol)
            names = []
    except ImportError:
        return {"status": "skipped", "raw": {"reason": "engine_unavailable"}}
    except ValueError as exc:
        return {"status": "error", "raw": {"reason": str(exc)}}
    except SyntaxError as exc:
        return {"status": "error", "raw": {"reason": "parse_error", "line": getattr(exc, "lineno", None)}}
    source_bytes = source.encode('utf-8'); digest = hashlib.sha256(source_bytes).hexdigest()
    spans = [{"id": relative.as_posix()+'::'+name+'/body', "start_byte": start,
              "end_byte": end, "source_sha256": digest}
             for name,start,end in omitted]
    if editable and suffix != '.py':
        return {"status":"skipped","raw":{"reason":"editable_python_only"}}
    records = []
    if editable:
        from rush.token_economy.ast_skeletonizer import signature_record
        records = [signature_record(source,relative.as_posix()+'::'+name,relative.as_posix())
                   for name in names]
    if editable and permissions is not None and permissions.cache_write:
        from rush.token_economy.ccr_store import CCRStore
        import json
        for record in records:
            tag = CCRStore(root).store_chunk(json.dumps(record,sort_keys=True))
            record['record_id'] = tag.removeprefix('<!-- ccr:chunk:').removesuffix(' -->')
    try:
        handle = persist_omitted(root, relative.as_posix(), source_bytes, spans, permissions) if recoverable else None
    except PermissionError:
        return {"status":"skipped","raw":{"reason":"cache_write_permission_required"}}
    return {"status": "ok", "raw": {"outline": outline, "omitted": spans, "handle": handle,
        "editable_records": records,
        "source_sha256": hashlib.sha256(source.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest(),
        "token_counter": "FastBPETokenCounter heuristic",
        "input_estimated_tokens": FastBPETokenCounter.count_tokens(source),
        "output_estimated_tokens": FastBPETokenCounter.count_tokens(outline)}}

# NEW helper in same module. Existing pinned tree-sitter==0.26.0 and
# tree-sitter-typescript==0.23.2 suffice for .ts/.tsx. Proposed
# pyproject.toml dependency line: "tree-sitter-rust==0.24.2"; regenerate
# uv.lock with `uv lock` when applying. Version/wheels verified on PyPI
# https://pypi.org/project/tree-sitter-rust/0.24.2/ ; ABI/runtime check below.
from tree_sitter import Language, Parser
import tree_sitter_typescript
def tree_sitter_outline(source, suffix, focus_symbol=None):
    if suffix == ".rs":
        import tree_sitter_rust  # proposed pinned dependency
        grammar = tree_sitter_rust.language()
        declarations, body_type = {"function_item"}, "block"
    else:
        grammar = (tree_sitter_typescript.language_tsx() if suffix == ".tsx"
                   else tree_sitter_typescript.language_typescript())
        declarations, body_type = {"function_declaration", "method_definition"}, "statement_block"
    data = source.encode("utf-8")
    root = Parser(Language(grammar)).parse(data).root_node
    if root.has_error:
        raise SyntaxError("outline parse error")
    definitions = []
    def visit(node):
        if node.type in declarations:
            name = node.child_by_field_name("name")
            body = node.child_by_field_name("body")
            if name is not None and body is not None and body.type == body_type:
                symbol = data[name.start_byte:name.end_byte].decode("utf-8")
                ancestor = node.parent
                while ancestor is not None:
                    if ancestor.type == "class_declaration":
                        owner = ancestor.child_by_field_name("name")
                        if owner is not None:
                            symbol = data[owner.start_byte:owner.end_byte].decode("utf-8") + "." + symbol
                        break
                    ancestor = ancestor.parent
                definitions.append((symbol, body.start_byte, body.end_byte))
                return  # body spans must not overlap nested definitions
        for child in node.named_children:
            visit(child)
    visit(root)
    wanted = focus_symbol.rsplit("::", 1)[-1] if focus_symbol else None
    matches = [item for item in definitions if item[0] == wanted or item[0].endswith("." + str(wanted))]
    if wanted and len(matches) != 1:
        raise ValueError("ambiguous_or_missing_focus:" + ",".join(item[0] for item in definitions))
    replacements = [(symbol, start, end) for symbol, start, end in definitions
                    if not wanted or (symbol, start, end) != matches[0]]
    for symbol, start, end in sorted(replacements, key=lambda item:item[1], reverse=True):
        data = data[:start] + (b"{ /* omitted */ }" if suffix != ".rs" else b"{ /* omitted */ }") + data[end:]
    return data.decode("utf-8"), [(symbol,start,end) for symbol,start,end in replacements]
```

```python
# src/rush/mcp.py::rush_token_outline
def rush_token_outline(path: str, focus_symbol: str = "", recoverable: bool = False,
                       editable: bool = False, allow_cache_write: bool = False) -> dict:
    from rush.token_economy.outline import outline_file
    from rush.permissions import ExecutionPermissions
    return outline_file(path, focus_symbol or None,recoverable=recoverable,editable=editable,
                        permissions=ExecutionPermissions(cache_write=allow_cache_write))

# src/rush/cli.py: replace both existing command definitions; same helper.
def _render_outline_cli(file_path: Path, focus_symbol: str, recoverable: bool,
                        editable: bool, allow_cache_write: bool) -> None:
    from rush.token_economy.outline import outline_file
    from rush.permissions import ExecutionPermissions
    result = outline_file(file_path, focus_symbol or None,recoverable=recoverable,editable=editable,
                          permissions=ExecutionPermissions(cache_write=allow_cache_write))
    if result['status'] != 'ok':
        click.echo(json.dumps(result,sort_keys=True),err=True)
        raise click.exceptions.Exit(1)

               else result['raw']['outline'])
```

**Actual capability:** Python AST transformation retains definitions/docstrings and replaces ordinary function bodies with ellipses; focused functions remain. Native Rush connector and fresh stdio MCP calls both returned a real Python outline.

**Reproduced defect:** TypeScript input is returned completely unchanged: wrapper omits language, defaults to Python, and parse failure returns original text. Polyglot fallback is a line heuristic. Correction to initial draft: current Python visitor implements both `visit_FunctionDef` and `visit_AsyncFunctionDef`; async support is not missing. Focus still matches only `node.name`, so identically named methods cannot be selected separately.

**Concrete patch specification:** Route MCP `rush_token_outline` and both Click outline aliases through the proposed `outline_file` above. Current `AstSkeletonizer.skeletonize` line fallback is insufficient even after passing the language: use installed `tree-sitter`/`tree-sitter-typescript` grammars for `.ts/.tsx`, and add a pinned Rust grammar for `.rs` before claiming Rust support. New `tree_sitter_outline` parses bytes, rejects `root.has_error`, discovers function/method `statement_block` spans, then replaces nonfocused spans from highest byte offset to lowest; a missing grammar returns `skipped/engine_unavailable`, never raw source as success. Python `ast.parse` errors propagate. Use `relative_path::Class.method` focus identifiers; an ambiguous short name returns candidate IDs without choosing. Preserve focused source bytes, and record tokenizer identity plus input/output token counts. The displayed helper is a proposed contract; parser traversal, Rust dependency, ToolResult adaptation and both route changes remain unimplemented.

Python `A.run`/`B.run` with focus `file.py::A.run` → focused statements retained (AST formatting may change), B omitted; async fixture follows same rule.     assert rush_token_outline(str(p))['raw']['reason']=='parse_error'
```python
    assert CliRunner().invoke(cli,['token','outline',str(p)]).exit_code==1
```

```python
# NEW helpers in src/rush/token_economy/outline.py, shared by MCP and CLI.
import hashlib
def recover_omitted(source: bytes, span: dict) -> bytes:
    if hashlib.sha256(source).hexdigest() != span["source_sha256"]:
        raise ValueError("stale_source")
    start, end = span["start_byte"], span["end_byte"]
    if type(start) is not int or type(end) is not int or not 0 <= start <= end <= len(source):
        raise ValueError("invalid_span")
    return source[start:end]
def persist_omitted(root, relative, source, spans, permissions):
    import json
    from rush.permissions import ExecutionPermissions, check_permissions
    from rush.token_economy.ccr_store import CCRStore
    allowed, missing = check_permissions(ExecutionPermissions(cache_write=True),permissions)
    if not allowed: raise PermissionError('recoverable outline requires '+','.join(missing))
    root = Path(root).resolve(strict=True)
    if hashlib.sha256((root/relative).read_bytes()).digest() != hashlib.sha256(source).digest():
        raise ValueError('stale_source')
    digest=hashlib.sha256(source).hexdigest()
    project_id=hashlib.sha256(str(root).encode()).hexdigest()  # X05 _context_identity.
    payload={'rush_context_version':1,'project_id':project_id,
             'sources':{relative:digest},
             'spans':[{'id':span['id'],'path':relative,'source_sha256':digest,
                       'text':recover_omitted(source,span).decode('utf-8')}
                      for span in spans]}
    tag=CCRStore(root).store_chunk(json.dumps(payload,ensure_ascii=False,sort_keys=True))
    handle=tag.removeprefix('<!-- ccr:chunk:').removesuffix(' -->')
    if len(handle)!=64: raise ValueError('invalid_ccr_handle')
    return handle
```

**New capability — editable outline with opaque bodies:** Current `rush_token_outline` only returns a read-only skeleton. Proposed `editable=true` returns signature records plus opaque body IDs. Agent sends a signature edit referencing the record; Rush reconstructs a real patch against original source without exposing or regenerating omitted bodies. Existing patch verifier checks that full patch. This directly enables edits from compact context; retrieval/citation metadata alone is not the feature.

**Exact ownership/wiring:** Add `signature_record` and `signature_patch` below to `token_economy/ast_skeletonizer.py`. `mcp.py:rush_token_outline` and both Click outline names accept `editable: bool=False`/`--editable`; when true, `outline_file` returns records for Python definitions along with outline. A read-only call returns records inline without storing. Persistent records require `ExecutionPermissions(cache_write=True)` and use existing `CCRStore(project_root).store_chunk(json.dumps(record))`; `record_id` is returned chunk hash. The existing patch-apply shared handler accepts `outline_edit={record_id,symbol_id,replacement_signature,expected_source_sha256}`; it loads record with `CCRStore.retrieve_chunk(hash,touch=False)`, checks source/path/hash, recomputes parser span, calls `signature_patch`, then passes returned unified diff through existing patch verifier. No production apply follows automatically. Model cannot supply arbitrary offsets: record and recomputation must agree. Unknown record or stale source fails before patch generation.

**Proposed replacement helper + runnable check** (not installed in Rush). Run together with `rtk proxy uv run --python 3.12 python -`:

```python
import ast, difflib, hashlib, io, tokenize

def signature_record(source, symbol_id, filename):
    tree = ast.parse(source); found=[]
    class Definitions(ast.NodeVisitor):
        def __init__(self): self.stack=[]
        def visit_ClassDef(self,node):
            self.stack.append(node.name); self.generic_visit(node); self.stack.pop()
        def visit_FunctionDef(self,node):
            found.append(('.'.join([*self.stack,node.name]),node))
            self.stack.append(node.name); self.generic_visit(node); self.stack.pop()
        visit_AsyncFunctionDef=visit_FunctionDef
    Definitions().visit(tree)
    prefix=filename+'::'
    if not symbol_id.startswith(prefix): raise ValueError('symbol_file_mismatch')
    matches=[node for name,node in found if name==symbol_id[len(prefix):]]
    if len(matches)!=1: raise ValueError('ambiguous_or_missing_symbol')
    node=matches[0]; tokens=list(tokenize.generate_tokens(io.StringIO(source).readline))
    keyword='async' if isinstance(node,ast.AsyncFunctionDef) else 'def'
    starts=[i for i,t in enumerate(tokens) if t.string==keyword and t.start[0]==node.lineno]
    if len(starts)!=1: raise ValueError('signature_start_unresolved')
    start_index=starts[0]; depth=0; end_token=None
    for t in tokens[start_index:]:
        if t.string in '([{': depth+=1
        elif t.string in ')]}': depth-=1
        elif t.string==':' and depth==0:
            end_token=t; break
    if end_token is None: raise ValueError('signature_end_unresolved')
    lines=source.splitlines(keepends=True)
    def offset(point): return sum(len(x) for x in lines[:point[0]-1])+point[1]
    start,end=offset(tokens[start_index].start),offset(end_token.end)
    return {'symbol_id':symbol_id,'source_sha256':hashlib.sha256(source.encode()).hexdigest(),
            'start':start,'end':end,'signature':source[start:end],
            'body_sha256':hashlib.sha256(source[end:].encode()).hexdigest()}

def signature_patch(source, *, record, signature, filename):
    if hashlib.sha256(source.encode()).hexdigest()!=record['source_sha256']:
        raise ValueError('stale_outline')
    current=signature_record(source,record['symbol_id'],filename)
    if current!={k:v for k,v in record.items() if k!='record_id'}:
        raise ValueError('record_mismatch')
    parsed=ast.parse(signature+'\n    pass\n')
    if (len(parsed.body)!=1 or
        not isinstance(parsed.body[0],(ast.FunctionDef,ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) or
        len(parsed.body[0].body)!=1 or not isinstance(parsed.body[0].body[0],ast.Pass)):
        raise ValueError('signature_only')
    candidate=source[:record['start']]+signature+source[record['end']:]
    ast.parse(candidate)
    if hashlib.sha256(source[record['end']:].encode()).hexdigest()!=record['body_sha256']:
        raise ValueError('body_changed')
    patch=''.join(difflib.unified_diff(source.splitlines(keepends=True),
          candidate.splitlines(keepends=True),fromfile='a/'+filename,tofile='b/'+filename))
    return candidate,patch

source = "def calculate(x):\n    # body never enters model context\n    return x * 2\n"
new_signature = "def calculate(x, *, trace=False):"
record=signature_record(source,'src/a.py::calculate','src/a.py')
candidate, patch = signature_patch(
    source, record=record, signature=new_signature, filename="src/a.py")
assert candidate[len(new_signature):] == source[record['end']:]
assert "+def calculate(x, *, trace=False):" in patch
original_ns, candidate_ns = {}, {}
exec(source, original_ns); exec(candidate, candidate_ns)
assert original_ns["calculate"](3) == candidate_ns["calculate"](3) == 6
try:
    signature_patch(source + "# changed\n", record=record, signature=new_signature,
                    filename="src/a.py")
except ValueError as exc:
    assert str(exc) == "stale_outline"
else:
    raise AssertionError("stale edit accepted")
```

**Additional integration acceptance:** Test nested methods, async/multiline signatures and decorators with parser-derived spans; `signature_patch` preserves existing indentation preceding `start` and candidate parse rejects malformed nesting. Changed source or unknown record fails before patch generation. Body suffix digest remains identical. Full patch must pass existing caller/API/regression checks before promotion. A default expression in a new signature may change behavior; unchanged body is not a behavior-preservation verdict. Measure total context and successful edit rate versus outline→full-file reread→edit.

## Command 59/79 — `rush_context_retrieve` (X05)

**Route and trigger:** `rush context retrieve HANDLE --json`; recover omitted evidence after context packing. MCP also accepts a project path. Sources: `mcp.py:142–148`, `cli.py:4114–4126`, `continuity/context.py:239–295`.

**Actual capability:** Reads an existing project CCR database, redacts recovered content, returns canonical continuity result with `recovered`/`not_found`; read does not initialize missing CCR storage. Optional cache-write controls touch and cost recording in the shared implementation.

**Issues:** Recovery has no token/byte budget, pagination or selective section input. It can return the full omitted payload that the preceding pack could not fit. Default-root retrieval also cannot find a handle written by the MCP pack's erroneous file-parent store (X08). Missing handles are `skipped`, which initialization text incorrectly equates to missing engines.

**Concrete proposed fix — replacement in `src/rush/continuity/context.py::retrieve_context`.** Reads the actual CCR database without initialization; binds cursor to project, stored chunk, selected spans and redacted payload; checks source freshness; budgets the complete serialized ToolResult. Cursor offsets are Unicode character offsets, not byte offsets. Old chunks without source identity require explicit historical retrieval. The minimum accepted budget is 512 tokens/2048 bytes; impossible metadata envelopes raise a budget error rather than silently exceed the cap.

```python
# Proposed additions/replacement in src/rush/continuity/context.py.
import base64
import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path
from time import monotonic
import tiktoken
from rush.continuity.results import build_continuity_result
from rush.safety.redactor import SecretRedactor
from rush.token_economy.ccr_store import CCRStore

def _context_identity(root):
    return hashlib.sha256(str(Path(root).resolve(strict=True)).encode()).hexdigest()

def _context_file(root, relative):
    root = Path(root).resolve(strict=True)
    path = root / relative
    resolved = path.resolve(strict=True)
    resolved.relative_to(root)
    if not resolved.is_file():
        raise ValueError("source_not_file")
    return resolved

def _wire_size(result):
    value = result.to_dict() if hasattr(result, "to_dict") else dict(result)
    wire = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
    return len(wire.encode()), len(tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base").encode(wire))

def _context_cursor(value):
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True).encode()).decode()

def retrieve_context(started, root, handle, granted, as_v1=False, *,
                     max_tokens=2000, max_bytes=16384, cursor=None, span_ids=(),
                     historical=False, invocation_id=None, project_id=None,
                     run_id=None, agent_id=None, session_id=None):
    root = Path(root).resolve(strict=True)
    if type(max_tokens) is not int or type(max_bytes) is not int or max_tokens < 512 or max_bytes < 2048:
        raise ValueError("context budget requires at least 512 tokens and 2048 bytes")
    identity = _context_identity(root)
    def output(reason, content=None, **extra):
        result = build_continuity_result(started, "ok" if content is not None else "skipped",
            reason, operation="context_retrieve", granted=granted, as_v1=as_v1,
            raw={"reason":reason, "content":content, **extra})
        if content is None:
            byte_count, token_count = _wire_size(result)
            if byte_count > max_bytes or token_count > max_tokens:
                result = build_continuity_result(started, "skipped", reason,
                    operation="context_retrieve", granted=granted, as_v1=as_v1,
                    raw={"reason":reason,"content":None,"metadata_truncated":True})
                byte_count, token_count = _wire_size(result)
                if byte_count > max_bytes or token_count > max_tokens:
                    raise ValueError("context budget cannot fit error envelope")
        return result
    database = root / ".rush/cache/ccr.db"
    if not database.is_file():
        return output("not_found")
    _context_file(root, ".rush/cache/ccr.db")
    with sqlite3.connect(database.resolve().as_uri()+"?mode=ro", uri=True) as conn:
        row = conn.execute("SELECT content FROM chunks WHERE hash=?", (handle or "",)).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        return output("not_found")
    original = row[0]
    if hashlib.sha256(original.encode()).hexdigest() != handle:
        return output("corrupt_chunk")
    try:
        payload = json.loads(original)
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        payload = None
    if not isinstance(payload, dict) or payload.get("rush_context_version") != 1:
        if not historical:
            return output("legacy_source_unverified")
        safe, _ = SecretRedactor.redact_value(original)
        payload = {"project_id":identity, "sources":{}, "spans":[{"id":"legacy","text":safe}]}
    if payload["project_id"] != identity:
        return output("wrong_project")
    stale = []
    for relative, digest in payload["sources"].items():
        try:
            current = hashlib.sha256(_context_file(root, relative).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            current = None
        if current != digest:
            stale.append(relative)
    if stale and not historical:
        return output("stale_source", stale_paths=stale)
    wanted = set(span_ids)
    available = {span["id"] for span in payload["spans"]}
    if not wanted <= available:
        return output("unknown_span")
    selected = [span for span in payload["spans"] if not wanted or span["id"] in wanted]
    safe, _ = SecretRedactor.redact_value("\n".join(span["text"] for span in selected))
    digest = hashlib.sha256(safe.encode()).hexdigest()
    binding = {"project_id":identity,"handle":handle,"payload_sha256":digest,
               "span_ids":[span["id"] for span in selected]}
    offset = 0
    if cursor is not None:
        try:
            value = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(cursor))
            offset = value.pop("offset")
            if value != binding or type(offset) is not int or not 0 <= offset <= len(safe):
                raise ValueError("cursor binding")
        except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError):
            return output("invalid_cursor")
    def frame(end):
        return output("historical" if stale or not payload["sources"] else "recovered",
            safe[offset:end], source_sha256=payload["sources"], span_ids=binding["span_ids"],
            next_cursor=_context_cursor({**binding,"offset":end}) if end < len(safe) else None,
            remaining_bytes=len(safe[end:].encode()), historical=bool(stale or not payload["sources"]))
    # Token counts need not be monotone under BPE. Shrink and measure the actual
    # complete frame; do not binary-search under an unproved monotonicity claim.
    end = min(len(safe), offset + max_bytes)
    result = frame(end)
    while max(_wire_size(result)[0]/max_bytes, _wire_size(result)[1]/max_tokens) > 1:
        if end == offset:
            raise ValueError("context metadata exceeds requested frame budget")
        end = offset + max(0, (end-offset)*3//4)
        result = frame(end)
    if end == offset and end < len(safe):
        raise ValueError("context budget cannot deliver next character")
    if granted.cache_write:
        # Constructor is reached only for existing DB and explicit write grant.
        CCRStore(root).retrieve_chunk(handle, touch=True)
        TelemetryStore(root).record_memory_event("handoff",
            len(tiktoken.get_encoding(_DEFAULT_ENCODING).encode(safe[offset:end])),
            request_id=handle, event_id=f"page:{offset}:{digest}", invocation_id=invocation_id,
            cache_write=True, **_memory_event_attribution(project_id,run_id,agent_id,session_id))
    return result
```
